Four optimization ports are integrated in maintained recipes, packaged resources
and catalog recognition. Fresh previews reproduce the accepted source artifacts
exactly. These are usable **source candidates**, not new rendering, visual-quality
or speed results. The nine-family, five-version, two-loader scope remains active.

## MakeUp UltraFast 9.5g: End clouds

The existing Overworld sample-budget mechanism now also reaches the default-active
End sky-cloud consumer: `world1/deferred.fsh → common/deferred_fragment.glsl →
volumetric_clouds_end.glsl:get_end_cloud`. Native ten iterations become nine with
Balanced and eight with generated Performance when Apply occurs in The End.
The existing renderer gate requires Overworld, so it does not bypass this End
shader consumer. Automatic route reselection after dimension travel is unverified.

The count changes before native stride calculation. Native slab endpoints,
dither, step-length weights, opacity normalization, first-contact shading and
final compositing remain. Quality/Off retain the original graph. The unchanged
helper rejects missing/unknown bridge and invalid inputs. Native AA is untouched.
Thin boundaries, nonconstant density and opacity caps can still change sampled
results; preserving interval and weights does not establish image equivalence.

Default one-read iterations imply ten → nine/eight cloud noise reads per eligible
ray; the two-read configuration implies twenty → eighteen/sixteen. Total-frame
benefit and hardware texture transactions are unknown. This is End coverage,
not an optimization of the existing Overworld workload.

## Complementary Unbound r5.9.3: primary-cloud density

BSL's native-zero detail-rejection principle now reaches Unbound's default
Overworld `deferred1` cloud density. Its four positive noise octaves use weights
1, .5, .25, .125 and exact normalization 1.875. Each octave makes two existing
explicit-LOD0 noise reads. After the first octave, the remaining weighted sum is
bounded by .875. A conservative .87501 remainder and negative .001 margin permit
returning zero only when the full native density cannot reach its positive-use
branch. Native sampling positions, march count, TAA, lighting, first-hit, opacity
and depth updates remain byte-identical.

For K reached eligible density calls and R certificates, nominal reads change
from 8K to 8K−6R; no prefix read is replayed. This can avoid six of eight density
reads on an empty sample. Reached R/K, compiler behavior, branch overhead and
whole-frame benefit are unmeasured. The certificate is a family-specific bound,
not a small-contribution threshold or a copied BSL equation.

Eligibility requires Balanced bridge2/enabled1, clear weather, primary Overworld
fragment deferred1, quality2/3 and native materials; DH/Voxy, generated normals,
coating, other passes, absent preset and invalid finite domains retain native
work. Existing noise sampling is unchanged. The pinned PNG noise path is
normalized; effective driver binding remains a runtime observation.

chat focuses on common LOD protocols. The overall product is configurable LOD
across many shader packs, using explicit adapters. Photon remains the reference
implementation. The latest authorization permits web research and exploratory

- Original chat owns common protocol/configuration: `src/main` config and Iris

- Fresh chat owns performance research, compatibility experiments, optional

- Coordinate through durable checkpoints before overlapping edits. Existing

- Keep one active project goal in STATUS/goals. A fresh native goal in the new

# Experimental frame-local shadow frustum coherence

Candidate implemented in isolated worktree
`/Users/pippo/.codex/worktrees/frustum-coherence/shaderlod` from `5a06ccd`.
Main checkout is untouched. After the coordinator released a CPU window,
`./gradlew build compileDevClientJava` passed with all 29 JUnit tests, including
nine new coherence fixtures. No game or benchmark was launched by this worker.
This is a default-off independent option, with no performance claim.

## What is avoided

Several Sodium section AABBs can occupy the same small spatial neighborhood
during one frustum traversal. A proven containing coarse box permits its valid
contained children to return visible without repeating all plane FMAs and
rejecting distance-box tests. Partial/outside/unproved coarse boxes still use
the exact original per-child path. No section is dropped, no shader budget or
radius is changed, and every visibility graph traversal still runs.

`ShadowFrustumCoherence` uses 64 fixed direct-mapped slots. The cell key comes
from each child minimum endpoint on a 64-block grid; its containing proof box
extends 96 blocks along each axis. Every call verifies actual float containment
and child finite/ordered endpoints before consulting a proof. Large boxes that
do not fit, NaNs/infinities, inverted endpoints and unknown/malformed planes
fall back. Hash collisions compare all three cell coordinates and never reuse
another cell's proof. Negative proof entries only avoid repeated coarse proof;
they never reject an individual child.

The helper owns three `int[64]` key arrays and one `byte[64]` proof array: 832
raw bytes plus headers/object fields, roughly 1 KiB per initialized frustum,
subject to actual JVM layout. It is lazily allocated on the first enabled
candidate test. There are no per-child allocations, reflection, config reads
or GL calls. New-frustum initialization still allocates this bounded storage,
which can be a material cost if Iris creates frusta every frame.

## Strict proof, rather than trusting Iris's INSIDE code

Pinned Iris's positive acceptance evaluates

`fma(px,x, fma(py,y, pz*z)) >= -pw`

while its negative/fully-inside expression folds `pw` into a third nested FMA.
Those have different rounding near the boundary. Its return value 1 cannot be
used as a general float-safe containment proof.

A concrete counterexample is plane `(1e20f,-1e20f,-1f,-0.5f)`, coarse AABB
`(1,0,0)..(2,1,1)`, and its contained point `(1,1,1)`. The original full
classifier can call the coarse box fully inside while rejecting the point,
under both FMA and separate arithmetic. A written test captures that behavior.

This candidate instead evaluates the **original positive expression** at the
coarse box's sign-selected minimum and maximum vertices, with the original
FMA policy and grouping. It requires finite plane coefficients and finite
results at both extrema, plus minimum result `>= -pw`. Finite contained child
positive vertices are bounded componentwise in the coefficient-selected order.
Float multiplication/addition/FMA with fixed finite coefficients preserve
that weak order; finite extreme evaluations exclude intermediate overflow/NaN
cases that could break the acceptance implication. Signed zero comparisons
remain Java `<0`, not raw sign-bit tests, and tangency remains inclusive.
Thus every accepted cached child satisfies its original positive acceptance
on every plane. Unproved values retain original behavior through fallback.

The coarse box must also lie **fully inside every rejecting distance box**:
each minimum at least `-maxDistance` and each maximum at most `maxDistance`.
Merely calling `BoxCuller.isCulledSodium(coarse)==false` would prove overlap,
not containment. The accessor reads the immutable pinned `maxDistance` field
without reflection. Missing primary cullers use an unbounded constraint;
NaN/negative limits cannot create a fast proof.

For reversed frusta, `distanceCuller` is rejecting, but the inherited primary
box is an **early acceptance**. A plane proof only needs the rejecting distance
constraint. When no proof exists, the original order remains distance reject,
alternate-box accept, then original classifier (or the separately enabled
old math experiment). The new option does not enable that older option.

## Lifetime and source integration

`ShadowCullingFrustumMixin` retains the pinned testAab fallback and adds a
coherence attempt before it only when the separate cached controller is active.
The base-injected interface exposes that helper to the reversed subclass,
avoiding inherited-shadow declarations in its child mixin.

The pinned `prepare` body first updates its box-culler position, then x/y/z.
The overwrite preserves that exact order and invalidates all slots. The pinned
private `addPlane(float[])` is the sole plane-array insertion/count mutator;
its overwrite preserves assignment/increment and invalidates proofs. Count,
plane-array reference, FMA policy or rejecting-limit changes also reset the
helper's context. Existing plane arrays are only populated during construction
in the inspected pinned implementation. Arbitrary external reflection or
third-party writes into private plane coefficients without these hooks are
not claimed supported; any such mutation producer would need explicit
invalidation before enabling the candidate in that combination.

No CallbackInfo/Operation wrapper is introduced by these overwrites. Inactive
paths add a cached boolean check and prepare/addPlane a nullable helper check;
that overhead is still unmeasured. No observer or timing-arm counters were added.

`rendering.shadowFrustumCoherence=false` is independent of
`rendering.optimizeShadowCulling=false`. The existing client tick performs
configuration/Photon/in-world/fallback checks for both and caches eligibility.
There is no temporal camera/sun key: prepare discards frame-local proofs, so
moving daylight does not depend on a previous frame's geometry. New frustum
objects start with no helper. `ShadowBoxDistanceAccessor` is registered against
the exact pinned Iris BoxCuller layout.

## Pending tests and acceptance

Nine written tests cover contained-child reuse, partial distance overlap,
invalidation/plane-limit-policy reset, direct-map collisions, finite/inverted/
NaN/infinity/signed-zero/extreme fallback, NaN/negative constraints, the INSIDE
counterexample, randomized original-classifier comparisons and reversed prefix
behavior. All nine passed. The property fixture exercises 5,000 plane sets × eight children ×
two arithmetic policies, and requires real fast accepts rather than vacuous
all-fallback success. The explicit INSIDE counterexample passed under both math
policies. These tests use an independent full pinned arithmetic oracle and
distance-box predicate; they do not establish runtime Mixin transformation or
actual scene plane/caster coverage.

Pinned-JAR signature inspection confirmed x/y/z are declared on the base target,
`maxDistance` is a private final double, and the sole addPlane/prepare bodies
match the copied ordering plus explicit invalidation. Production jar inspection
confirmed the helper/accessor are present and developer classes excluded.
Then the coordinator must validate actual
Mixin application and original-versus-enabled ordered section/caster sets in
the same frame, motion, plane tangency, day/night, reloads and optional DH/stack
variants. Default off, coherence on, and old math on are separate controls.

Only then benchmark repeated serial frame/CPU results with original Photon
quality and radius unchanged. Coarse misses/collisions, first-proof work,
allocation per new frustum and containment/hash overhead can outweigh avoided
plane math. A source operation reduction or passing property fixture is not
proof of a useful frame gain. No shadow list/temporal traversal reuse is enabled
by this independent experiment.

## Implementation and source contract

Pinned Sodium 0.6.13 `RenderRegion` owns one persistent mutable
`ChunkRenderList`. Its public constructor takes `RenderRegion`; the getter
returns that original list. Pinned Iris 1.8.12 has separate outer shadow lists,
but collector membership still aliases those region objects. Exact source
revision, local ignored review files and annotated bytecode are recorded in
`VISIBILITY_REUSE_AUDIT.md`.

New production components:

- `ShadowListStorage<T>` holds the original and lazily constructs one alternate
  shadow list. There is no static owner map or saved world/manager reference.
- `ShadowRegionListsMixin` overwrites only Sodium `RenderRegion.getRenderList`.
  Disabled/main paths return the original field. An active shadow getter lazily
  creates owner-local storage and `new ChunkRenderList(thisRegion)`.
- `ShadowVisibilityListsController` caches one active boolean. Per-region
  getters perform no config/Iris pack inspection, GL call or reflection.
- `ShadowVisibilityListsRuntime` reads config and existing Photon names once
  per client tick, requiring global enablement, an in-world shader pack,
  recognized Photon and no Iris fallback.
- `rendering.separateShadowVisibilityLists=false` is the new experimental
  default. NeoForge's client tick listener and both mixins are registered.
  Sodium's pinned artifact is added to main compile-only inputs; its runtime
  remains required by Iris exactly as before.

Lists are owner-local and allocated only on the first eligible shadow visit.
The noncapturing constructor function is initialized once on the transformed
class, not per getter. This adds a storage object, one shadow list and its three
`byte[256]` arrays per shadow-visited region; roughly 0.9–1.1 KiB per region
with typical compressed-reference HotSpot layout, an estimate pending actual
heap inspection. Main/disabled getters retain the original object identity.
Disabling/re-enabling keeps the same alternate storage for that live region;
forced traversals still repopulate it. World/manager replacement constructs
new regions/storage, allowing the old graph to be collected normally.

## Exact existing sprite-consumer behavior

This requirement prevents a superficially correct list split from silently
changing animated-shadow texture activation.

Pinned `RenderSectionManager.tickVisibleRenders` iterates its **main outer
container**, even during shadow setup. In the original shared-list design,
regions visited during that shadow traversal have their inner arrays overwritten
with shadow membership; regions not visited keep their preceding main data.
Regions not in that main outer container are not visited by this sprite tick.

`ShadowSpriteListsMixin` redirects only its
`ChunkRenderList.sectionsWithSpritesIterator()` invocation. In an active shadow
phase, for each existing main-container entry it returns the shadow iterator
only when that owner's alternate list has the current manager
`lastUpdatedFrame`. Otherwise it returns the original main iterator. The caller
continues using the same region and same section/sprite iteration. Main and
disabled paths invoke the original iterator directly. No region is added to
the outer container; no stamp is rewritten; no sprite is ticked by a new hook.

provenance. It is not a change to "tick all shadow sprites" or broad animation
policy. Frame-wrap equality follows the same original integer-generation
comparison; no elapsed-time or camera-distance substitute is introduced.

intervals include driver/command gaps, not busy-time utilization. Per-run p95,

# Shared shader LOD decisions

The shared mechanism wraps the existing uniform-free
[`effect_policy.glsl`](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/effect_policy.glsl)
numerical engine. It does not choose a pack preset or infer a distance from depth.
The Java `DistanceBands`/`EffectPolicy` semantics remain the policy oracle. No
upstream shader attribution was removed; these files contain ShaderLOD mechanism
code and no copied Photon algorithm.

Entry points are
[`shaderlod_work_decide`](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/work_policy.glsl)
and [`shaderlod_shading_rate_decide`](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/shading_rate.glsl).
Include `work_policy.glsl` first; it explicitly includes the maintained common
`effect_policy.glsl`. Include `shading_rate.glsl` only for a spatial consumer.
The archive assembler must copy these named common sources into `/include/shaderlod/`.
There are no uniforms, options, samplers, derivatives, frame selectors or projection
assumptions. Helpers use GLSL 4.10-compatible constructs.

`ShaderlodWorkPolicy` supplies these fields:

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `core_version` | Must be 2; missing/unknown versions retain original work. |
| `effects_version`, `minimum_effects_version` | Extension 1 or 2; the consumer requires 1 for an original effect group or 2 for OpaqueLighting. No forward-version guess. |
| `global_enabled` | False retains original work. |
| `mode` | 0 INHERIT, 1 FULL, 2 ADAPTIVE; unknown values retain original work. |
| `inherited_policy_resolved` | Mode 0 may use supplied bands/ratios only when the consumer explicitly resolved its existing inherited policy. Otherwise full. |
| `policy_enabled` | False retains original work. For ADAPTIVE, normally true after the adapter's explicit gate. |
| `bands_blocks` | Radial camera-relative Euclidean near/far/full centered transition width in Minecraft blocks. |
| `retained_ratios` | Medium/far fraction of the actual upstream work count, with `0 <= far <= medium <= 1`. Never radiance, density, radius or effect strength. |

The adapter also supplies `capability_valid` (pinned revision, explicit operation,
transport/capability schema and distance source), `quality_valid`, `protected_work`,
distance, its actual upstream count and legal floor. Quality validity and protection
must be established before expensive consumer work. The common mechanism does not
fetch textures to discover those inputs. Near/invalid/member protection may be
supplied explicitly; absent proof of quality must supply `quality_valid=false`.
Protected shadow/AO budgets still permit separately declared exact work reuse.

The underlying transport-safe numerical domain is unchanged: far <= 4096 blocks,
width <= 512 blocks, positive width >= 1/1024 block, distance <= 16777216 blocks,
count <= 16777216. Invalid or unsupported values retain the caller's original
count, including an invalid negative count; callers must preserve their original
path rather than loop over malformed inputs. This narrower domain is explicit;
the Java API accepts other finite distances and larger integers.

Transitions match the Java model: 32/96/8 has centered intervals 28–36 and 92–100.
Before the first interval the ratio is 1. Zero width changes tiers exactly at the
boundary. Touching transitions are allowed; overlapping/negative/nonfinite bands
are rejected. The helper does not reinterpret the near boundary or substitute
thresholds. A consumer requiring full work through a larger near region supplies
its own declared protection guard.

`ShaderlodWorkDecision` separates:

- `retained_ratio`, `medium_blend`, `far_blend`: continuous distance request.
- `continuous_requested_work`: binary32 upstream × ratio before legal floor.
- `continuous_work`: continuous request clamped to the legal floor and upstream.
- `requested_work`: upward integer rounding before legal floor.
- `realized_work`: integer count after legal floor, bounded by upstream. This is
  negotiated numerical work, not evidence of executed GPU operations.
- `upstream_work` and `reason`: original count and eligibility/fallback diagnostic.

Reasons are POLICY=0, INVALID=1, GLOBAL_DISABLED=2, FULL=3,
UNRESOLVED_INHERIT=4, EFFECT_DISABLED=5, PROTECTED=6, UNSUPPORTED=7,
QUALITY_FALLBACK=8. Numerical/protocol validation precedes other reasons; a valid
disabled/full/protected/unsupported path returns unity ratio, original counts and
zero transition weights. The original/mod-absent and disabled baseline therefore
retains the pack's selected upstream operation. Binary32 arithmetic can cross an
integer threshold relative to Java doubles; tests explicitly bound that difference
rather than claim bit-exact driver execution.

## Concrete continuous volume call

The existing primary volumetric integration is the bounded reference consumer.
Construct `ShaderlodWorkPolicy` from its resolved core/effect controls, actual
upstream integration count and minimum legal cells. Call:

```glsl
ShaderlodWorkDecision work = shaderlod_work_decide(policy,
    declared_volume_capability_valid, interval_and_quality_valid,
    protected_volume_view, radial_entry_distance_blocks,
    int(original_cells), int(minimum_cells));
```

`radial_entry_distance_blocks` must be the length of a camera-relative entry
position in blocks, with any adapter origin shift applied explicitly. A volume
endpoint's view Z or a surface depth alone does not establish this distance.
`interval_and_quality_valid` must include the existing finite positive interval,
resolved feature scale, final-pixel footprint and protected-view weight checks.
A typed capability schema may provide `shaderlodCapabilitiesVersion == 1 &&
shaderlodVolumeIntegrationAvailable == 1`; only the explicit adapter declares
those uniforms and validates its pinned source/options.

For the existing footprint/protected-view quality refinement, retain its declared
weight `footprint_weight * (1 - protected_weight)`, mix the full upstream target
toward `work.continuous_requested_work`, then apply its legal floor. Do not replace
this continuous target with `work.realized_work`: the existing
`shaderlod_volume_cell_length` and `shaderlod_volume_cell_sample` preserve the
whole integration interval with a last partial cell. A full fallback target must
select the original integration path, preserving jitter, density/extinction,
normalization and early exits. Continuous work is quadrature budget, never
extinction/scattering strength. A hard protection guard returns full before that
refinement. The consumer connection and its exact entry program remain root-owned;
this source freeze does not prove consumption.

## Discrete spatial rates

The optional rate helper takes a work decision, region member count, supported
mask, region validity and protection. Legal region sizes are 1, 4, 16. Rate side
lengths are 1, 2, 4; retained evaluations are 1, 1/4, 1/16 respectively. Mask bits
1/2/4 declare those rates; full rate bit 1 is mandatory. Region size and count
must agree with the upstream work decision. The legal floor must also permit the
requested rate's exact evaluation count.

`requested_rate=0` means an intermediate continuous request is unsupported.
There is no snapping or dithering. An unsupported intermediate, missing declared
rate, insufficient region size, quality failure or protected member realizes rate

## Why the earlier cuts lost structure

The maintained unprotected PCF patch caps medium at four/two taps and far at one.
Far uses a center offset and replaces the initial-four test with the reduced
count. One bilinear comparison covers its local texel footprint rather than the
original disc: it can miss nearby thin caster coverage and replace an area-average
penumbra with a binary-looking result. Receiver distance or a subpixel projected
penumbra does not bound that difference. TAA may reduce stochastic noise; it does
not guarantee reconstruction of removed coverage.

Aggressive far GTAO returns AO=1/ambient SSS=0 with the view normal as bent normal;
SSAO returns 1. These are missing lighting contributions, not just fewer samples
of the same estimate. Sparse SSRT misses occluders in its larger gaps. The user
observed missing distant tree shadows and rejected roughly 0.5 ms saved; the
agent had underemphasized flatter foliage. The cited earlier AO pass interval was
only 0.057 ms and is workload/instrumentation qualified, not a universal budget.
See [the recorded lesson](USER_LESSONS.md). Do not attribute the observed failure
to PCF alone: several lighting paths changed together.

The recent exact GTAO depth-reuse pilot retained arithmetic but regressed in its
single, qualified forest block. It gives no accepted gain and warns against
assuming texture-fetch reuse beats native caching/register costs. Its focus and

## Reusable eligibility and error rule

A future explicit adapter should carry three pieces of information locally:
camera-relative distance, the **projected filter footprint**, and a bound on
the **lighting-result error**. Distance gates importance; footprint describes
sampling; error determines whether removing work is permissible. None is a
replacement for the other two. No capability registry or new uniform protocol is
needed to investigate this rule.

For a flat receiver, analytically project two receiver-tangent offsets into
display pixels and distorted shadow texels, obtaining two 2×2 Jacobians. Their
composition maps a display-pixel displacement into shadow texels. Invert it to
estimate the filter disc's major/minor radius in display pixels. Use the actual
viewport/FOV/TAAU scale and light projection; do not treat block distance or map
resolution as a screen-footprint proxy. Invalid/singular transforms, grazing
receivers, large Jacobian variation over the filter, depth/material discontinuities
or missing DH projection support select the original path. Capture derivatives
before divergent control flow if derivatives replace the analytic construction.

An initial investigational gate would keep full original work through the entire
near band and permit scrutiny only beyond the far band's end (100 blocks for
32/96/8), with projected major radius below 0.5 display pixel. These are conservative
starting thresholds, not accepted optima. Even when that gate passes, an additional
error certificate is required. The original filter radius, all sample positions,
weights, sharpening and comparison depth stay fixed. Do not shrink a disc to
manufacture a subpixel footprint or substitute a center sample.

One concrete certificate is possible **if** the actual opaque comparison sampler
performs bounded bilinear interpolation of four depth-comparison results at a
fixed reference depth. In shadow-texel units, that scalar result has slopes bounded
by one in each axis. Reusing a fetched value at another coordinate therefore has
ideal interpolation error at most the coordinate L1 separation `delta_i`.
Require complete valid footprints, fixed map/reference depth, verified filtering/
comparison/wrap modes and a separately established hardware precision allowance
`eta`; otherwise use the original fetch. Same texel cell alone is insufficient.

Keep the original first four comparisons and early-exit decision byte-identical.
For each remaining comparison, reuse a previous fetched value only while
`sum(delta_i + eta) <= N * epsilon / G`, where `N` is the unchanged original count
and `G=1/(1-2*a)` is the actual sharpening gain. Photon clamps its sharpening
threshold `a` to at most 0.4, so `G<=5`. Normalize by the original N and run the
original sharpening. This bounds the ideal scalar visibility deviation by
epsilon even for an arbitrary thin caster pattern; empirical hardware precision
and final lit-color perception still need separate acceptance. A fresh fetch
resets the cached coordinate/value, not the cumulative per-filter error budget.

Start with an investigational epsilon no larger than 1/255 in visibility, full
near/original fallback and default-off source selection. That value is not a
perceptual guarantee: direct-light intensity/specular response can amplify it.
Approximate reuse remains a quality change and must not bypass default lighting
protection. With protection enabled, only genuinely identical coordinates and
reference inputs may qualify for exact reuse; do not declare a nonzero epsilon
safe under the existing protected flag. INHERIT/FULL/unknown extension versions,
missing mod or unsupported sources preserve their defined original behavior.

## Candidate: preserve rays and stop only bounded scattering tails

First adapt the cumulus series only, under a new private default-OFF gate and
known existing core/global bridge. Scope to `PROGRAM_DEFERRED1`; unknown controls,
invalid/negative inputs, unsupported paths and sky-map rendering retain all eight
orders. Preserve primary locations/counts, cloud density, direct/sky optical-depth
marches, transmittance/extinction, apparent distance, phase noise, buffers and
temporal reconstruction. Surface lighting and shadows remain original.

Compute the first four orders exactly. At this single stopping point, use the
known state to bound orders 4–7. Let `A_j` be the positive scattering amplitude,
`p_j` powder, `f` the original fixed scattering falloff, and `g_j` the original
three HG anisotropies for order j. The exact amplitude recurrence is

`A_(j+1) = A_j f p_j`, `p_(j+1) = (p_j + sqrt(p_j))/2`.

For `|g| < 1`, the exact HG maximum over cosine in [-1,1] is

`Hmax(g) = (1 + |g|) / (4π (1 - |g|)^2)`.

Use `Pmax_j = .65 Hmax(gx_j) + .10 Hmax(gy_j) + .25 Hmax(gz_j)`.
The actual anisotropy contracts by .8 per order in cumulus. With nonnegative
optical depths/extinction, all exponentials are at most one. For cumulus
shadow parameter `s` in [0,1] and nonnegative bounced light `b`, conservative
pre-integral tail bounds are

`Bx = Σ[j=4..7] A_j ((1-.5s) Pmax_j + (b+.5s)/(4π))`

`By = Σ[j=4..7] A_j/(4π)`.

These are finite four-term bounds; do not assume an infinite geometric series
with ratio .55. The powder factor starts as high as π and can make early
amplitudes grow. A cheap alternative is to use the order-4 phase maximum for
all four terms: subsequent absolute anisotropies shrink and their HG maxima
cannot increase. The finite amplitude sum still uses the exact powder recurrence.

Only stop if both bounds are below 2% of their respective already-computed
positive four-order components; otherwise finish the exact eight-order series.
Use a stricter threshold initially if desired, without claiming that HDR error
directly equals perceptual error. The threshold is a diagnostic adapter policy,
not an existing mod-config field or verified product connection. A common work
policy can later supply a retained order cap/error budget after usefulness is
demonstrated; do not build that interface first. A distance policy can restrict
eligibility further but cannot replace the contribution bound.

The common step integral and primary transmittance multiply both the original
and tail. Under positive inputs, this retains the same component-relative bound
after summing those cells along a ray. It bounds the untonemapped scalar direct/
ambient channels. It does **not** certify displayed RGB: Photon can extrapolate
color saturation, later filtering/history and exposure can amplify perceptual
differences, and separate lightning ambient data consumes the Y component.
Qualify nonnegative finite inputs or fall back. Preserve both channels, including
stored indirect scattering, instead of assuming ambient light is invisible.

The source-only model checks 36,288 synthetic cumulus input combinations and
72,576 component inequalities against the finite envelope. At thresholds 2%,
5%, 10%, respectively 4,249 / 6,366 / 9,614 grid cases pass the bound. These are
grid counts, **not a predicted runtime eligibility fraction**. Density, optical
depths and weather inputs are independently enumerated, not measured correlated
cloud cells; calculations use Python double precision rather than driver GLSL
float. GLSL needs finite guards, outward rounding/safety margin and its own
fixtures before claiming a conservative implementation.

A concrete blind-cut falsifier: density .5, cosine 0, all optical depths 100,
extinction/scattering coefficient .05, shadow .5, bounced light .1. The exact
scalar recurrence loses up to 40.52% of a component when cut 8→4. The model's
maximum component loss is 99.82% at an extreme sky optical depth; that number
does not establish whole-image damage but refutes a universal small-tail claim.
Higher orders have weaker extinction and supply dense-cloud fill. A naive
distance-only cap is therefore rejected even though direct shadow marches remain.

## Cost ceiling and fail-fast acceptance

Per occupied cumulus primary sample, original source has four exponential sites
per order: 32 for eight orders, 16 for four. Altocumulus has three: 24→12, if a
later separate adaptation is worthwhile. Original multiple-phase calls after
orders update three HG lobes; useful updates after orders 0–6 can fall from
seven to three. The final unused update may already be removed by the compiler.
Primary and secondary density invocations/fetches are unchanged. The bound adds

instruction savings or a throughput prediction. Cumulus repeats the same sky
exponential in its X and Y expressions; the compiler may already share it.

## Spatial and temporal inputs

The fine texture coordinate is `(pos + 0.4*wind)*0.005`; the coarse detail texture
uses `(pos + 0.2*wind)*0.0009`. Each is 64³ and repeats. At scale 10, fine lattice
spacing is `1/(64*0.005*10) = 0.3125` camera/world blocks; coarse lattice spacing
is about 1.736 blocks. Full repeat periods are 20 and 111.111 blocks. These are
source coordinate/lattice scales, not a proof that nonlinear density is strictly
band-limited. Density squares detail, erodes coarse coverage and applies a
rational contrast function, so a texture-cell Nyquist argument alone is unsafe.

`wind = wind_velocity*world_age`; prior `pos` translation plus the fine term gives
1.4 times wind velocity in fine coordinates. Fine lattice motion is
`64*0.005*1.4*|wind_velocity|` texels per world-age second. Actual camera motion
adds relative motion. `world_age=((worldDay%128)*24000+worldTime)/20` can wrap;
frozen benchmark world time does not test normal cloud-wind evolution. Keep
upstream checkerboard phase, jitter, temporal history and reset behavior.

Use the actual cloud viewer `air_viewer_pos` and **current density evaluation
point**, including secondary-ray points, to compute observer distance divided by
`CLOUDS_SCALE`. Do not use fragment terrain depth, planet radius, `length(pos)`,
or distance from the first shell sample. Upstream primary `ray_origin` is already
at the shell entry plus jitter; its `distance_to_sample` omits camera-to-shell
distance and is unsuitable as the LOD metric.

Derive a conservative pixel cone from neighboring unprojected normalized rays,
using the same selected vanilla/DH projection and TAAU scale as the main ray.
For point distance `s` in atmosphere units, transverse footprint is approximately
`s*max(length(dir_x-dir), length(dir_y-dir))`. Multiply by `0.005*64` for fine
texture-cell coverage. Compute directions explicitly before marches; use no
screen derivatives within divergent ray loops. Start with **one final display
pixel**, not the 4×4 checkerboard tile, so retained temporal detail is protected.

Primary linear step length and secondary exponential step lengths are known at
their callers. They are longitudinal integration spacing, not pixel-cone width.
Preserve them; do not enlarge the cone by `max(pixel_width, ray_step)` and assume
the resulting isotropic density average preserves optical depth. Secondary points
use the observer cone at their own position while retaining all light-ray inputs.

## B21 — remaining-radiance termination

For an extinction-weighted integrator, a valid tail decision must bound both
unintegrated in-scattering and the error in transmitted background. If prefix
transmittance is `T`, a loose per-channel bound is
`T * (maximum_remaining_source_radiance + maximum_background_radiance)` when
the remaining scattering albedo and visibility are bounded by one. Pack
multipliers, phase functions and exposure/tonemapping must also be bounded.
For example, `T=0.001` with background radiance 1000 permits a radiance error
of 1 merely from dropping the remaining attenuation; the small T alone says
nothing useful about display error. This is a counterexample, not a measured
scene radiance or chosen threshold. Bloom, exposure and extra alpha consumers
must have their own bound. Additive visibility sums need a weighted *remaining
sum* bound; inventing a T accumulator changes the native algorithm.

# Benchmark guide

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

On Linux ARM64 use `python3 scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py benchmark test` with the same arguments. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

idle slots are fine. Parallelize independent source/cost research and minimal
implementation only when warranted. GPU/client is serial and has one owner.

dependencies, acceptance evidence, stopping boundary and report destination.

The human requested this model; other workers/coordinator inherit their defaults.

## Development discipline and communication

Use minimal explicit patches and existing bridges. Prototype to reject ideas
quickly; don't build a general framework before a successful consumer. Do not
reopen rejected extra-pass spatial/cache paths without materially new evidence.
Test the actual producer report shape and runtime option discovery before an
expensive capture. Inspect actual exit/result files; modeled tests do not prove
runtime. Run relevant checks once, then move to the decisive experiment.

Reuse qualified identities while preserving exact immutable source/artifact pins
and explicitly known startup normalization. Do not weaken guards to pass. Avoid
new redundant identity schemes. Keep raw failures, versions, settings and inputs.
Distinguish correctness, activation, quality, physical work and measured speed.
Commit coherent source only if useful, with short messages and no coauthors;
no remote push/publish, credential changes, installs or unrelated job changes.

At every meaningful decision, update a compact current-state block at the TOP
of STATUS and a bounded milestone in the existing goal. Link historical details
instead of copying them into both files. State current objective, best evidence,
owners/live jobs, blocker, hypothesis and next decisive action. No competing
task database or mandatory new failure document for every run.

In interactive turns give a meaningful update about once a minute. During
unattended continuation notify only on an accepted result, important directional
change, failure needing human action, completion or essential decision. Every
30 minutes of active work internally ask whether the last interval delivered a
measurement, eliminated a material hypothesis or fixed a necessary prerequisite.
If none, narrow or stop the lane; do not call activity progress. Never guarantee
a speedup before evidence or quietly reduce the quality requirement.

Scopes and limitations:

- Frame wall: interval between normal `GameRenderer.render` starts, including
  scheduling, swap/limiter and instrumentation outside the renderer region.
  The first interval after an epoch change is unavailable. FPS is reciprocal
  mean frame wall time, not a mean of instantaneous reciprocals.
- Renderer wall and current render-thread CPU: HEAD to every normal RETURN of
  the pinned renderer method. Rendering GUI is part of this scope.
- Process CPU: all JVM threads during that renderer region, from
  `OperatingSystemMXBean.getProcessCpuTime`, when supported.
- GPU: actual asynchronous desktop OpenGL `GL_TIME_ELAPSED` queries over the
  renderer region. GL33 or ARB_timer_query and positive counter bits are required.
  Existing active elapsed queries are respected; no overlapping query is opened.
  Ring pressure, zero results, query timeout and unsupported APIs are explicit.
  Pending queries are polled for availability without blocking and deleted on
  epoch invalidation/close. Stale results cannot move into a new phase.
- Nanoseconds are storage units; effective clock precision is platform/driver
  dependent. Counter width is recorded separately and is not claimed as 1ns
  resolution. Disabled instrumentation uses one request branch and performs no
  clock/query work after shutdown of its prior active epoch.

## Entry points, counters and units

Trace is private/default OFF. The selected code requires
`SHADERLOD_WORK_TRACE`, Overworld `PROGRAM_DEFERRED1`, and absence of
`ATMOSPHERE_TRANSMITTANCE_LUT`. Entry is
`shaders/world0/deferred1.fsh` → `program/d1_clouds.fsh` → `draw_clouds` →
`draw_cumulus_clouds`. Original/global-OFF fallback uses Photon cumulus; adapted
execution uses `shaderlod_volume_draw_cumulus` in the
[diagnostic adapter copy](../shaderpacks/photon-shared-work-trace/shaders/include/shaderlod/photon_volume_trace_adapter.glsl).

The common trace is initialized once per fragment. Increments occur at reached
operations, including early density returns; they do not derive work from the
requested cap, density strength, final radiance or history.

| Counter | Exact unit |
| --- | --- |
| Primary iterations | Reached primary loop body after the transmittance-break check, before adapted partial-cell rejection |
| Density evaluations | Cumulus density function entries, both primary and secondary, including shell/coverage/altitude early zero returns |
| Secondary visits | Reached optical-depth loop bodies, lighting and sky; excludes the eight-iteration scattering approximation |
| Texture evaluations | Reached texture-value calls in cumulus density/local coverage: local coverage map, both Worley fields, or two procedural coverage reads |

Texture counts exclude `textureSize`, depth/dither samples, other cloud layers,
crepuscular rays, atmosphere and post-lighting work. They are source-level
texture evaluations, not hardware fetches or instruction counts. The secondary
unit is deliberately narrower than all secondary arithmetic.

Page 1 records the original primary budget and the actual selected draw body's
continuous target. `requested_work` means the target supplied to that draw,
including existing footprint/protection restoration; it does not expose the
unprotected policy ratio or preflight request. Original uses N/N/N; adapted
uses N/target/target. Coverage-zero exits occur before upstream computes N and
retain initialized zero budgets, while the known selected path is recorded.
Path 0 means no cumulus draw; 1 means original/fallback; 2 means adapted; 3 is
reserved and unused. Reason 0 is the only emitted reason: individual wrapper
fallback causes are not classified. This boundary is explicit in the metadata.

## Why prior defaults did not establish the goal

Historical global OFF/ON same-JVM controls showed approximately 6–11% GPU reductions
in some native workloads, while the original/disabled/enabled five-effect pilot
regressed active GPU time by 6.76% forest and 0.82% coast. These have different
controls and must not be combined into an accepted original-versus-active gain.
Reduced far SSR controls changed sign or were flat, and a bright water band exposed
quality problems. Cloud consumer/extent/literal probes supplied no useful
incremental gain. These are recorded results; they do not prove a single cause.

Potential explanations needing measurements include work in protected lighting
remaining at upstream cost, sparse effect coverage, texture-cache reuse, branch
divergence and savings being dominated by unchanged passes. The matched-source
coastal pass-timed versus frame-only pair (23.8452 versus 14.8650 ms) raises an
instrumentation concern. One separate-JVM pair does not establish its cause or
absolute pass shares. Do not rank effect costs from that inflated profile.

The goal's target is at least 33.333% lower total frame time for 1.5x throughput.
If an effect occupies fraction `f` of GPU time and reduces its cost by fraction
`r`, its idealized GPU reduction is only `f*r`; CPU and other unchanged frame work
further constrain total-frame improvement. Neither fraction is measured for this
probe. Exact fetch reuse is the first correctness test, not a numerical promise.

Private option `SHADERLOD_AO_DEPTH_REUSE_PROBE` defaults off. With the option off,
selecting its preprocessor branches restores all original source bytes. With it
on, the uniform-coherent dispatcher calls the cache kernel only when
`shaderlodBridgeVersion == 2 && shaderlodEnabled == 1`. Absent/unsupported bridge,
global OFF, and malformed enable values call the retained original kernel. Only
these two existing fields are consumed; new per-effect API/transport is not
connected to this probe. No per-effect ratio, preset, near/far or debug consumption
is inferred from uniform declarations.

The original `compute_maximum_horizon_angle` remains byte-for-byte intact. The
cache kernel duplicates it and changes only the depth-fetch site plus cache state:

1. Convert the original clamped ray position to the original integer texel.
2. Reuse the previous scalar depth only when that texel is in texture bounds and
   matches the immediately previous valid texel.
3. Otherwise execute the original `texelFetch` inside the miss branch. Invalid
   texels always fetch and clear validity: upstream out-of-range results are
   undefined, so their repeatability is not assumed.
4. Run every original early continue, fractional-coordinate reconstruction,
   falloff, cosine maximum and angle conversion without modification.

The AO pass reads combined depth but writes AO/history buffers 6/14. Under the
pinned source's read-only depth binding, repeated valid level-zero texel fetches
return the same value; sampler derivatives/filtering do not enter `texelFetch`.
Cache state is local to one horizon ray, cannot survive frames/reloads, and is
updated before early continue. Cache reuse never drops an iteration or substitutes
the previous fractional ray position. Driver compilation and output parity still
need runtime checks; source equivalence cannot guarantee driver optimization.

Distance remains upstream camera-relative view-space block units. This exact
reuse has no distance cutoff or transition band: projected sample spacing makes
it naturally relevant where texels repeat. Changing the global gate or projection
changes only reuse opportunities, with expected unchanged lighting output. No
frame-random selection or new dither is introduced. Unknown inputs preserve the
original kernel; undefined edge fetches preserve original behavior by bypassing
the cache. Quality fallback is full original lighting, never AO=1 or missing
shadows. The new effect-policy owner agrees that exact reuse is a separate
capability from quality-budget cuts, so lighting preservation may remain enabled.

compile-time unrolling. Original actual call-site counts are compile-time pack
options, which makes constant propagation/specialization possible. B15's actual
counts depend on distance/noise/preset. Whether the driver specializes, unrolls,
or uses rolled loops remains unknown.

For each reduced secondary invocation the added source contains one inequality
branch, two `exp2` calls, two ratio divisions and scalar conversion/arithmetic,
in addition to the original base-length division. This occurs twice per
nonempty primary sample. One `exp2` input is an original pack constant and may
fold; the count expressions are ray-invariant and may hoist or simplify. Those
are source-expression counts, not a claim that four physical exponentials are
issued per primary sample.

The three `shaderlod_budget` calls are before the primary loop, not inside it.
They use `lod.glsl:79–85`: tier-zero return, preset lookup, nested scale selection,
ceil and min/max. Mode 0 compile-time selection excludes the alternative
overhead-geometry/mode-1/mode-2 block; functions present elsewhere in the ZIP do
not prove their execution. Cached-sky-off returns tier zero for its fixed-origin

# Development shadow input observer

The observer records shadow transform/input equality and a limited projected
motion proxy. It never cancels rendering, skips clears, changes matrices,
modifies textures or authorizes shadow reuse. Production mod sources and jar
remain separate from this development source set. Its motivation and the
transaction hazards are in [PHOTON_SHADOW_CACHE_DESIGN.md](PHOTON_SHADOW_CACHE_DESIGN.md).

Enable only for a separate diagnostic capture:

```text
-PshadowObserve=true
```

The coordinator maps that property to
`shaderlod.dev.shadowObserve=true`. Default is false. Disabled hooks return
original expressions/matrices immediately before reading game inputs; recording
entrypoints perform no work, GL calls, allocations or clock reads. Disabled
`snapshot()` returns a cached report object. Preallocated arrays and that object
are allocated once at class initialization, not during frame recording.

## Registration and report API

Register these dev mixin class names in `shaderlod-dev.mixins.json`:

```text
ShadowInputObserverMixin
ShadowMatrixObserverMixin
```

Mixin registration and `WorkloadSession` wiring are coordinator-owned. Public
API on `com.pp.shaderlod.dev.timing.ShadowInputObserver`:

```java
configurePhotonFeatures(Map<String, String> effectiveOptions);
beginMeasurement();
Snapshot snapshot();
```

Call configuration once with the actual loaded Photon option map, then
`beginMeasurement()` at capture start and `snapshot()` for report serialization.
Missing/non-boolean WAVING_PLANTS, WAVING_LEAVES, WATER_DISPLACEMENT,
WATER_CAUSTICS or COLORED_LIGHTS entries remain unknown. Configuration allocation
and report/map allocation happen outside frame hooks. The snapshot excludes the
current pending renderer frame, which completes at the next observed renderer
start; it does not finalize or mutate rendering state. Starting measurement
excludes any pending warmup frame and discards earlier comparisons.

The frame ID comes from the existing development `GpuTimers.beginTick()` counter,
which advances independently of whether GPU queries are enabled/sparse. Duplicate
or nonconsecutive render frame IDs are reported rather than treated as adjacent
comparisons. The observer is intended for the coordinator’s ordinary single-view
client-thread captures; VR/multiple-view semantics require another audit.

## Pinned source hooks and side-effect boundaries

Audited Iris jar: `iris-neoforge-1.8.12+mc1.21.1.jar`, SHA1
`a3e6355915c7d3b2bc392724795113e51d289378`. Hooks are strict (`require=1`,
`expect=1`) on that binary; a different version needs source/runtime checks.

`ShadowInputObserverMixin` uses MixinExtras `ModifyExpressionValue`, returning
the identical original value. It observes the first `Minecraft.getInstance()`
expression inside `ShadowRenderer.renderShadows`, after the zero-shadow-distance
early return and before shadow renderer mutation. It reads existing camera
position/angles/entity, world day/game time, render directives and resolution.
`SystemTimeUniforms.TIMER.getFrameTimeCounter()` is a side-effect-free field
getter in the pinned bytecode; it does not advance the timer or reevaluate a
smoother/uniform supplier. No world/entity/chunk enumeration or reflection occurs.

At the second `LevelRendererAccessor.getLevel()` invocation within the slice
after `ShadowCompositeRenderer.renderAll()`, it observes completed geometry and
existing `ShadowRenderer.MODELVIEW`/`PROJECTION` floats plus rendered entity/block
entity counts. At this point Iris has restored its GL/render buffers/culling and
cleared ACTIVE. The early-zero-distance path does not pass through these hooks
and therefore contributes no renderer frame; it is not represented as a reused
map. Exceptions/incomplete paths never produce certified completeness.

`ShadowMatrixObserverMixin` uses `ModifyReturnValue` on the pinned methods:

```text
MatrixUniforms.lambda$addMatrixUniforms$0(PackDirectives): Matrix4fc
MatrixUniforms.lambda$addMatrixUniforms$1(PackDirectives): Matrix4fc
```

These are the original model-view/projection supplier bodies. Each handler
returns the same matrix reference without modification and does not call the
supplier again. All return calls during an active observer frame are counted;
only the first return for each matrix kind is copied. Renderer matrices and
consumer supplier matrices are separate observations. Missing probes or source
versus first-consumer disagreements are explicitly reported. It does not claim
that every program supplier was inspected or that later evaluations cannot
change. No extra JOML matrices/CallbackInfo objects or varargs arrays are created
by these hooks; the observer uses fixed primitive arrays and scalar operations.

## Reading the report

- `completedFrames` and `comparablePairs` count valid observed renderer frames
  and adjacent pairs with complete finite matrix probes and stable world/renderer
  identity. Missing probes, incomplete frames and identity/frame gaps are recorded.
- `observedEqualPairs` / `observedInputEqualityFraction` describe equality of
  the observed camera/world clocks/matrices/caster counts. They are **not cache
  hit rate or eligibility**. `exactReusableFrames` always stays zero.
- `changeCounts` overlap: camera origin/pose, clock/game tick, render/consumer
  transforms, light-orientation 3×3 matrix, caster counts, identity/gaps,
  missing/nonfinite inputs and source/consumer disagreement. Parent reasons are
  not exclusive categories; do not sum them into a frame count.
- `blockerCounts` fail closed for unobserved terrain/mesh, material/texture,
  callback and view/caster-visibility inputs. Player/entity/block-entity render
  directives block unobserved poses even when rendered counts are zero. Waving,
  caustics/voxel writes, unknown flags and unobserved weather inputs are distinct
  blockers. Equal positions/counts never establish equal poses, alpha or wind.
- `projectedReferenceDeltaTexels*` compares seven static world anchors using
  observed `projection × modelView`, remapping current camera-relative coordinates
  to the previous world origin. The anchors are the origin and ±32 blocks X/Z,
  ±16 blocks Y. Delta is converted from undistorted NDC to shadow texels at the
  observed resolution. Photon nonlinear distortion, caster silhouettes, receiver
  coverage, frustum changes, texture alpha and wind displacement are excluded.
  Quarter/one-texel counts are diagnostic proxies, not quality guarantees.
- `potentialTwoFrameCadencePairs` counts only the projection proxy ≤0.25 texel
  and observed renderer spacing ≤8.333333ms. It excludes no dynamic-caster or
  fidelity risks and does not simulate skipped frames. It indicates a narrow
  geometric/scheduling opportunity to investigate, not demonstrated savings.
- `engineBeginFinalizeMeanMs/MaxMs` measure the engine’s begin/finalize work with
  `System.nanoTime()`. They exclude mixin game-field reads, supplier handlers and
  matrix recording, and are neither total overhead nor CPU-thread time. Actual
  enabled/disabled runtime overhead still needs matched capture measurements.

Wetness/biome values, resource/source revisions and full caster poses are not
observed here. Reusing the wetness tracker report alongside this observer is
useful context but does not close those gaps. No exact eligibility switch exists
in the observer API, so a caller cannot turn an identical-input observation into
a rendering permission.

```sh
java -cp build/dev-shadow-tests com.pp.shaderlod.dev.timing.ShadowObservationPolicyTest

```

These pass disabled gating, observed equality with exact eligibility still
blocked, camera-relative coordinate cancellation, projected texel scaling,
light rotation and input reason separation, identity/frame isolation, missing
and nonfinite probes, warmup reset, player/waving/voxel/unknown flag blockers and
single-copy supplier gating. Build/source checks do not establish mixin
application or actual in-world overhead.

Coordinator runtime checks, still pending at implementation handoff:

2. Confirm both mixins apply without selector failure and renderer/consumer probes

# DH replacement coverage audit

Audited 2026-10-04 against the locked
`DistantHorizons-3.3.3-1.21.1-fabric-neoforge.jar`, SHA1
`4357b4d19fab818780c94f0e43dad1cc931634b2`. This audit used `jar tf` and
`javap -c -p` on that artifact. Online API documentation is supporting context;
it can change independently of the pinned binary. No new in-world acceptance
or automatic coverage guarantee is established by bytecode inspection.

## What the public API establishes

`DhApi.Delayed.configs` and `worldProxy` can be null before initialization.
`IDhApiWorldProxy.worldLoaded()` establishes world readiness. On
`IDhApiGraphicsConfig`, `renderingEnabled()`, `renderingMode()` and
`chunkRenderDistance()` establish enabled normal rendering and configured reach.
The controller checks these cached reflection handles on client ticks only.
`EDhApiRendererMode` in the pinned jar has `DEFAULT`, `DEBUG_TRIANGLE` and
`DISABLED`; only `DEFAULT` is eligible. DH configured reach must be at least the
uncapped requested vanilla radius. Neither these values nor warmup prove data,
meshes or successful draw coverage.

The public [terrain repository API](https://distant-horizons-team.gitlab.io/distant-horizons/com/seibel/distanthorizons/api/interfaces/data/IDhApiTerrainDataRepo.html)
can return terrain columns/regions. In the pinned implementation,
`DhApiTerrainDataRepo.getDataPointsAtPos` obtains
`IDhLevel.getFullDataProvider().getAsync(position)` and then calls
`CompletableFuture.get()`. Cache misses can therefore block on storage/provider
work. These queries are not used in the tick or Options getter. Even complete
repository data would establish source availability, not completed render
conversion/upload or correct render-list selection.

`IDhApiTerrainDataCache` only exposes `clear()` and `close()`; it has no public
coverage query. `IDhApiRenderProxy` exposes texture identities, renderer metadata,
transparent-pass controls and cache clearing, with no complete uploaded-section
coverage enumeration. A valid depth texture cannot certify the replacement ring.

`DhApiBeforeBufferRenderEvent.EventParam` supplies `modelPos`, in addition to
[render matrices and level information](https://distant-horizons-team.gitlab.io/distant-horizons/com/seibel/distanthorizons/api/methods/events/sharedParameterObjects/DhApiRenderParam.html).
It does not identify section detail/extent, missing terrain columns, or complete
360-degree coverage. Observing visible-buffer events would omit culled sections
and cannot establish safety when the camera turns. No buffer-count threshold is
used as coverage proof.

## Internal seams for future research

The pinned `LodRenderSection` has `pos`, `renderDataDirty`,
`renderBufferContainer`, `canRender()`, `gpuUploadComplete()` and rendering-enable
state. Bytecode shows `canRender()` only tests whether the buffer container is
non-null; `gpuUploadComplete()` tests container presence and `!renderDataDirty`.
These names alone are not proof of every terrain column existing, active
quadtree selection, or a complete ring under all views.

`RenderBufferHandler` owns `lodQuadTree` and exposes `getColumnRenderBuffers()`.
A robust version-pinned integration could investigate the client quadtree's
selected complete sections and their source completeness, conversion/upload
state, render-enabled selection and ring overlap. This would require independent
synchronization/thread-lifetime analysis and cold-cache/moving-camera tests.
Do not enumerate mutable renderer structures opportunistically in an Options
getter or equate a database hit with an uploaded render buffer.

## Implemented conservative alternative

The terrain feature remains default-off with explicit scene acknowledgement.
`GeometryCoverageGuard.Scene` binds world, Iris pipeline, camera entity, 16-block
X/Z cells and Y section, requested radius, cap and configured DH radius. Initial
true acknowledgement waits until a stable eligible scene has completed warmup,
so ordinary startup with no player/pipeline does not consume the confirmation.

After binding, mismatched or unavailable scenes revoke acknowledgement until
false→true confirmation. Crossing an X/Z chunk or vertical-section boundary
restores the original effective distance immediately in the getter; its local
revocation also survives an excursion-and-return between ticks. There are no
config reads, reflection, allocations, GL calls or renderer reloads there.
Tick-time invalidation covers readiness, normal rendering mode, DH reach,
pipeline/world/camera changes and radius/cap changes. The original Options
preference is never rewritten, and a lower server/manual radius is never raised.

Chunk/section boundaries provide a deliberately small, fixed guard around a
manual warmed view. They do not establish safe arbitrary travel: sub-cell
movement, third-person camera displacement, terrain edits, mesh-quality
changes and independent cache clearing remain risks. Automatically re-arming
on elapsed time would hide those risks, so this implementation does not do so.

## Acceptance evidence and remaining runtime checks

`./gradlew compileJava test --tests com.pp.shaderlod.GeometryLodPolicyTest
--console=plain` passes ten tests covering eligibility, restoration, startup,
scene invalidation, between-tick revocation, negative coordinates and reach.
That establishes source/build/unit behavior. The coordinator owns runtime checks:

- Start with persisted true, fixed camera, DH normal mode/reach128 and requested
  vanilla24: stay24 during warmup, then reach cap16 after a settled inspected view.
- Move across an X/Z chunk or Y-section boundary: return24 immediately; move back
  and wait: remain24. Explicit false→true after inspection can restore16.
- Reload shader pipeline, switch world/dimension/camera, change cap/request/DH
  distance or disable normal DH rendering: fail open and require new confirmation.
- Remove DH entirely, disable ShaderLOD/terrain/shaders, or trigger Iris fallback:
  retain current original effective radius without optional-DH class loading failure.
- Inspect water, shadows, seam overlap and cold terrain while rotating/moving;
  measure only after any Sodium rebuild/upload transition settles.

A successful checklist still validates an acknowledged scene policy; it does not
make automatic terrain coverage an implemented feature.

## Concrete 26.3 API consequences and sharing boundary

[NeoForge's 26.3 primer](https://docs.neoforged.net/primer/docs/26.3/)
documents the rendering API move from Blaze3D to Renderpearl (`api`, `frontend`,
`backend`), removal of output texture overrides, explicit render-pass attachments,
and SDL3 replacing GLFW. GPU buffers become interfaces; pipeline/uniform layouts,
bind groups and push constants change. Existing GLFW F8 registration must use
current `InputConstants`/SDL scancodes. An existing GLFW focus/timing probe cannot
be accepted unchanged.

[Mojang's 26.3 release](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-java-edition-26-3)
documents ShaderC for vanilla shaders on both backends, `#include`, explicit
input/output locations, rearranged Globals/DynamicTransforms uniform blocks,
multi-draw terrain and OIT passes. This applies to vanilla shaders; inspected Iris
still uses its own OpenGL compiler for pack shaders. Shared compile assumptions,
UBO offsets, depth conventions or the old transparency chain are unsafe.

Current project seams requiring target-specific work:

- `src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/mixin/CommonUniformsMixin.java` and Fabric's
  `FabricCoreUniformsMixin.java`: Iris `generalCommonUniforms` hook remains in the
  examined source, but old main-target width/height and integer GL texture IDs
  need replacement with current target/texture objects and certified identity.
- `IrisWorldCompletionMixin.java`: `finalizeLevelRendering()V`, `updateNotifier`
  and final composite/final-pass ordering remain in examined 26.x source;
  source preservation is not successful mixin injection or temporal correctness.
- `integration/IrisRuntimeAccess.java`: effective options, dimensions, fallback
  and pipeline status need exact-version compilation and loaded-path validation.
  `KnownRuntimeBoundary.java` reads GL driver strings and must run only on GL.
- `fabric/ShaderLodFabric.java`: GLFW key constants must change for 26.3.
  Shadow/Sodium internals require their own exact 0.9.2 audit.

Reuse the existing pure work-budget decisions, immutable settings/capabilities,
source pins and reversible pack-generation/ownership policy. Keep loader events,
UI/input, camera/target identity, linked uniforms, frame completion and backend
resource lifetime in small explicit version/backend adapters. No general GLSL
rewriter or new universal renderer framework is justified by this inspection.

There is no verified Iris Vulkan graph seam, so no Vulkan optimization or speed
prediction is proposed. To support Vulkan with the existing packs, the orchestrator
must choose a supported shader backend/API with concrete source, shader-pack
semantics and loader support, or coordinate upstream work. That is an unresolved
architecture decision, not a silently accepted dependency substitution.

# Explicit adapter target and pass layout

2026-10-05. The dependency-free
[`layout`](../src/main/java/com/pp/shaderlod/lod/adapter/layout/AdapterLayout.java)
API validates immutable, adapter-supplied image allocations, quantity views,
reads, simultaneous draw groups and full-target viewports. It complements the
[work adapter contract](LOD_ADAPTER_CONTRACT.md) and
[spatial pipeline](SPATIAL_LOD_PIPELINE.md). It contains no pack names, attachment
indices, GLSL parser, rewriting, source discovery or automatic source certificate.
An accepted declaration proves structural consistency of that declaration only.

The motivating diagnostic failure resized target 11 while a later upstream draw
still bound targets 11 and 12 at different dimensions. A producer-only target
check would miss this conflict. Adapters must declare **every reachable draw
group**, including preserved upstream groups. The validator compares every
attachment to the first, including a third or later attachment; it never stops
after one matching pair.

| Declaration | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `Dimensions` | Positive integer level-zero image or viewport dimensions. |
| `TargetSize.Absolute` | Fixed allocation dimensions. |
| `TargetSize.Relative` | Independent rational width/height scales of the rendered surface, each with explicit FLOOR or CEIL. |
| `TargetDeclaration` | Namespaced logical image identity, size, reviewed format and one or more quantity views. |
| `Quantity` | Namespaced basis/schema key, storage role, required channels and, for bounded float integers, an explicit maximum magnitude. |
| `PassDeclaration.Read` | Explicit image identity and numeric/unfiltered fetch declaration. |
| `PassDeclaration.DrawGroup` | Attachments simultaneously drawn with one viewport. Separate groups may use different dimensions. |
| `AdapterLayout` | Immutable targets and ordered pass declarations. Duplicate target/pass identities are schema errors. |
| `LayoutValidation` | Immutable resolved target dimensions and located failures; `valid()` means no structural failure. |

Sizes use actual rendered surface dimensions, not display size. Positive int
scale terms multiply in long; even maximum int terms plus the CEIL adjustment
fit long. Resolution rejects zero after FLOOR and any result above
`Integer.MAX_VALUE`, rather than truncating or wrapping. At 1709 × 961,
CEIL half/quarter allocations are 855 × 481 and 428 × 241. This matches the
spatial kernel's allocation formula; incomplete receiver tiles still require
the adapter's full fallback. A declaration can never prove that shader mapping.

Every group must have equal attachment dimensions and a viewport equal to those
dimensions. Smaller viewports fail `VIEWPORT_UNDERSIZED`; larger ones fail
`VIEWPORT_OVERSIZED`. A viewport smaller on one axis and larger on another reports
both. Partial draws, atlas region offsets and mip/subresource layouts are outside
this initial contract. Do not suppress this full-target check to authorize them.
Unknown read/write identities and failed allocation formulas invalidate the
layout; remaining independent checks still run.

Direct read/write overlap is rejected under `FeedbackPolicy.UNSUPPORTED`.
`DISTINCT_IMAGES_EXTERNALLY_VERIFIED` declares that the same logical identity
uses **physically distinct** read/write images, for example reviewed ping-pong.
It never authorizes sampling the same image being drawn. The adapter/runtime
owner must establish those distinct images; the validator cannot inspect GL
bindings, aliasing, pass completion or renderer flip/clear behavior.

## Storage and exact certificates

Each quantity view declares its own channel requirement; views can occupy
different texels of one allocation. Their channel counts are not summed. Packing,
locations, lifetimes, units and decode remain explicit adapter obligations.
Known formats are deliberately reviewed enum entries; unsupported formats need
an explicit API extension and checks, rather than inference from shader text.

`R11F_G11F_B10F` is a reviewed packed RGB floating format: stored component widths
11/11/10, no sign bits, 5 exponent bits and 6/6/5 stored fraction bits.
[`Khronos specification`](https://registry.khronos.org/DataFormat/specs/1.4/dataformat.1.4.inline.html)
defines these unsigned mini-float encodings. `componentBits(channel)` exposes each
width; scalar `componentBits()` returns the minimum width (10 for this format,
unchanged for existing uniform-width formats). It permits a three-channel float
quantity, has no stored alpha and cannot satisfy any exact metadata or binary32
distance role. The adapter must separately prove the quantity's nonnegative range
and acceptable rounding error; a linear declaration alone makes neither claim.

- `GENERAL` checks channel capacity; `LINEAR_QUANTITY` also requires float storage.
  Neither validates that a shader expression is a linear basis.
- `EXACT_SIGNED_INT32_METADATA` / `EXACT_UNSIGNED_INT32_METADATA` require matching
  32-bit integer storage and signed/unsigned integer `texelFetch` declarations.
  RGBA16I, floating point and signed/unsigned reinterpretations fail.
- `BINARY32_MINIMUM_DISTANCE` requires 32-bit float storage and
  `Fetch.FLOAT_TEXEL_FETCH`. Half-float or filtered reads cannot certify an exact
  conservative minimum. Raw float bits stored in integer metadata instead use
  the exact integer role; preservation via `floatBitsToInt` / `intBitsToFloat`
  remains source/driver proof.
- `EXACT_BINARY32_BOUNDED_INTEGER_METADATA` requires an explicit maximum integer
  magnitude in **[1, 16777216]**, 32-bit float storage and
  `Fetch.FLOAT_TEXEL_FETCH`. Every integer in that signed magnitude interval is
  representable in binary32. 16777217 is not; it rounds to 16777216. Ordinary
  float storage does not automatically grant this metadata role. Fractional,
  out-of-domain, stale or misdecoded shader values are not inspected by Java.

`FLOAT_OR_NORMALIZED` declares ordinary float/normalized reads; it cannot read
integer textures or satisfy exact float metadata/distance fetch requirements.
The integer fetch variants declare unfiltered integer addressing. Actual shader
instructions and runtime texture/sampler state must separately match declarations.

# Conditional normal variance and roughness transfer

2026-10-05. Owner`procedural_lod`; mathematical advisor`procedural_lod/parallax_math`.
New files only: common`normal_variance.glsl`, `tests/test_normal_variance.py`, this
report. Frozen Photon adapters, builders, manifests, mod config and consumers
remain untouched. **No shader entry point consumes this helper yet.**

A reusable conditional covariance-to-NDF-width helper is implemented and tested.
Its assumptions do **not** currently support a proved, useful Photon water
compensation: missing phase/covariance statistics, strong anisotropy and Photon’s
mirror water reflection path remain unresolved. Keep actual water normal reduction
unaccepted. The helper is an experimental quality mechanism, not a performance
result or a guarantee of highlight energy/width.

## Primary-source basis and model boundary

Han et al. formalize normal filtering as convolution of the normal distribution
with the BRDF; replacing detail by an average normal alone loses shading information.
Their high-frequency representation retains more than one normal lobe when needed.
[Frequency Domain Normal Map Filtering, authors’ paper](https://www.cs.columbia.edu/cg/normalmap/normalmap.pdf).

Olano/Baker’s LEAN mapping keeps first/second slope moments in a common tangent
frame, including anisotropic highlight shape, rather than treating every normal
map as an isotropic scalar roughness. Their posted errata also distinguish variance
combination from the final normalized Beckmann shading expression.
[LEAN Mapping, authors’ page and errata](https://userpages.cs.umbc.edu/olano/papers/lean/).

Trowbridge–Reitz/GGX has long slope tails; its NDF and masking model together
determine the BRDF. Changing a normalized NDF’s width alone does not establish
conserved observed radiance. [PBRT microfacet theory](https://www.pbr-book.org/4ed/Reflection_Models/Roughness_Using_Microfacet_Theory).
Reviewed primary engine code explicitly discusses missing GGX second moments and
uses different approximations for normal filtering and finite-tail conversion;
there is no universal variance coefficient to copy blindly.
[Unity CommonMaterial source](https://github.com/Unity-Technologies/Graphics/blob/master/Packages/com.unity.render-pipelines.core/ShaderLibrary/CommonMaterial.hlsl).

No code was copied from those sources. The Gaussian model and explicit radial
GGX truncation below are stated mathematical models; neither certifies Photon’s
area-light/Smith/Fresnel/clamped response. Research was browsed for this task.
The historical Pixar paper URL redirected to a research-library landing page;
that redirected page is not used as evidence for an unseen equation.

## Helper contract and exact fallbacks

`shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/normal_variance.glsl` takes a verified
removed tangent-slope covariance `(xx,xy,yy)` in **dimensionless slope-squared
units**, where slope=`normal.xy/normal.z` in a common orthonormal frame. It takes
upstream NDF width**alpha**, not alpha² or perceptual roughness. No camera-distance
units or automatically guessed statistics are embedded.

`shaderlod_normal_variance_removed(C,w)` returns `(1-w²)C` for a known independent
centered contribution retained with weightw. This is the loss of field variance;
`(1-w)²C` describes the difference/error field and is a different quantity. For
multiple correlated octaves, the caller must instead provide the complete
C_full−C_retained including cross-covariance. Negative eigenvalues are rejected,
not clamped into artificial roughness.

`shaderlod_normal_variance_alpha(...)` selects one explicit model:

- Mode1, Gaussian/Beckmann slope moment addition: alpha_new²=alpha_old²+2v,
  where v=trace(C_removed)/2. This exactly matches the isotropic Gaussian slope
  width within that model. If anisotropy is merely small rather than zero, replacing
  it by the trace is an approximation controlled by caller eligibility limits.
- Mode2, **opt-in experimental** radial-truncated GGX moment matching. Full GGX
  has divergent slope second moments, so a finite radial massq is explicitly chosen.
  Mode2 is rejected unless`allow_ggx_approximation` is true. Matching that finite
  moment is not the exact convolution of GGX with a filtered normal field.

For normalized isotropic GGX slope density
`p(s)=alpha²/[pi(alpha²+|s|²)²]`, a radial cutoffR retains
q=R²/(alpha²+R²). Direct integration gives conditional per-axis variance

\[
v_q=\alpha^2 c(q),\qquad
c(q)=\frac{-\log(1-q)-q}{2q}.
\]

The experimental mapping uses alpha_new²=alpha_old²+v/c(q). This is a radial,
conditional finite-domain convention. It is not interchangeable with marginal-axis
cutoffs, a quoted retained-mass percentage from a different convention or the
Gaussian factor2. Changing q changes the fitted width. Helper q is restricted to
0.5..0.999; q=1/full variance is rejected.

| Chosen radial massq | v_q/alpha² |
| ---: | ---: |
| 0.50 | 0.1931471805599453 |
| 0.90 | 0.7792139405522478 |
| 0.94 | 0.9964950621064019 |
| 0.99 | 1.8258435282768135 |
| 0.999 | 2.9573349744655335 |

The helper returns the original alpha plus`accepted=false` for disabled/near/full,
unverified moments, unpreserved mean slope, unsupported material, unstable frame,
grazing light/view, nonfinite/singular/invalid covariance, excessive variance,
excessive anisotropy, unsupported model or excessive alpha change. Covariance
must be positive semidefinite; intrinsic per-axis variance ceiling0.01 restricts
this small-slope candidate. Alpha is restricted to0.0001..1. Caller limits can be
stricter; failing them retains original work rather than clamping a supposed
energy correction. Invalid upstream alpha itself is retained with rejection,
not silently repaired into another material.

**On rejection, the adapter must keep original normal detail before skipping it.**
Applying roughness after already discarding rejected detail would violate the
fallback. Eligibility/moments must therefore be resolved before expensive-octave
work. The common helper performs no sampling, derivatives, implicit-gradient
lookup, removed-octave evaluation or uniform/config transport.

Transitions come from continuous removed covariance as normal weights vary.
There is no distance policy in this helper. An adapter must bring its removal
proposal smoothly to zero before grazing/material/variance eligibility boundaries;
the helper’s rejection flag is not a temporal-transition implementation. At a
near/full/disabled boundary, original alpha and original normal work are required.
