| surface/water_normal.glsl | `a6d2dc6bed11d723e5468e22f46b9d8c2fdb090a3e2e1b5131ff1759e89849d3` |

Photon `Material.roughness` is alpha: both highlight and reflection compute its
square for the GGX distribution/Smith terms. Lab material decoding already squares
perceptual smoothness complement. Base water alpha is0.002; water texture highlight
adds0.3×texture_highlight, so0.002 is a base value, not every pixel’s final alpha.
Do not square an already-alpha material again when passing it into this helper.

`get_specular_highlight` bends NoH using a spherical area-light approximation,
uses Fresnel and Smith visibility, and caps output at4 to control bloom. These
nonlinear operations matter to both peak brightness and integrated visible energy.
A pure NDF-width match does not undo their effects after changing normals.

More decisively, rough-SSR VNDF sampling is inside`if (!is_water)`. Water remains
on the mirror ray`reflect(world_dir, normal)` even when rough reflection support
is present. Adjusting material alpha changes some weighting but cannot reconstruct
the distribution of reflected directions lost by removing water normal detail.
When rough-SSR support is absent, crossing roughness0.05 also changes f0/SSR fade.
Thus modifying the shared water material roughness can introduce additional
reflection brightness changes. Direct-highlight-only compensation would still
leave the altered mirror direction and needs separate quality proof.

## Why amplitudes alone do not supply actual moments

For an ideal uniform phase and a **known fixed** phase incrementδ, Photon’s wave
has centered autocovariance

\[
C(\delta)=\tfrac18\cos\delta+\tfrac1{128}\cos2\delta,
\quad
S(\delta)=\tfrac14(1-\cos\delta)+\tfrac1{64}(1-\cos2\delta).
\]

With original normalized amplitudeA_i, constant height multiplierV, influenceI
and finite-difference steph=0.1, per-axis slope variance is
`(I*A_i*V/h)²*S(delta_axis)`. Smallδ approaches the derivative estimate
`S≈(5/32)δ²`; the exact finite-difference formula handles larger frequencies.
The two-axis covariance is C(δx−δy)−C(δx)−C(δy)+C(0).

Actual Photonδ includes the unknown difference of the omitted octave’s noise
sample atq+h andq, not just carrier frequency. Uniform phase, fixed V, independent
phase/noise and cross-octave independence are unverified. Height variation uses
related noise; it changes both covariance and mean-field terms. A carrier-only
prediction therefore cannot set`moments_verified=true`.

For a carrier-only third-octave illustration, N3/persistence0.5/ordinary influence
0.04/V1 gives covariance
`(2.8828907158232084e-05, -5.442597072792424e-05, 0.00012920358593251457)`.
Its anisotropy ratio is0.9369399027097054, so a scalar policy with threshold0.1
rejects it. Ignoring that issue and applying the Gaussian trace formula would raise
base alpha0.002 to0.01272919844651448. This is an **unvalidated model illustration**,
not predicted actual Photon roughness or accepted distant highlight preservation.

Scalar reference sampling of actual pinned noise/height functions exposes the
cross-covariance problem directly. Over48 still-water5×5 patches (step0.125blocks,
N3/p0.5/influence0.04/times0/17/113), full-minus-first-only covariance is indefinite
in17 cases. Example origin(7,13)/time0 gives
`(-4.253866899432137e-06, -3.796483565642477e-05, 0.00014931809433425976)`,
with minimum eigenvalue−1.3126601926179536e-05. Removing detail can increase variance
in an axis because of cross-correlation; positive roughness broadening cannot
represent that tensor. These are finite scalar reference patches, not sampled
GPU pixels or a population estimate. They disprove automatic independent-positive
variance addition for those fields. Removed waves were evaluated **offline in
fixtures** to check the model, not inside the helper’s proposed rendering path.

Second moments also do not fix arbitrary highlight shape: two synthetic isotropic
fields with identical means/covariance but different higher moments give GGX slope
peak responses30.594952535927593 and39792.63624702275, a1300.6275× difference at
alpha0.002. This is an unclipped slope-density counterexample, not Photon output
brightness. It explains why moment matching requires an explicit distribution
approximation and cannot prove peak/energy parity for a non-Gaussian wave field.

## Static acceptance, cost and adapter stopping boundary

Executed`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_normal_variance.py -v`:
**12 tests passed, no skips**. Fixtures cover Gaussian width addition, correct
weight² variance transfer, finite radial GGX integral/normalization and divergence,
higher-moment peak counterexample, finite/PSD/magnitude/anisotropy/material/grazing/
near/full fallback, finite phase moments and actual pinned water/SSR/alpha source.
Actual pinned Iris option lexer reports no helper references/options; its bundled
GLSL4.10 syntax parser accepts the helper. No full shader-stage consumer transform,
GL driver compilation, linked uniforms, rendering, reload, motion, GPU counters or
performance measurement ran on this track.

Cost includes finite/PSD checks, one covariance discriminant norm, one alpha square
root and, only in opt-in GGX mode, one logarithm. Model scale can be precomputed per
material. No such mod transport/adapter consumption exists. Any statistics capture
or precomputation needed to provide trusted moments has its own cost; this helper
does not hide it behind a late rendering branch.

The bounded next adapter plan is conditional, not authorization to modify the
frozen water probe: establish zero-mean/common-frame statistics and C_full−C_retained
at the actual pixel footprint, including phase/height variation/cross-covariance;
reject unsupported/multimodal/anisotropic/grazing cases before choosing normal LOD;
calibrate direct GGX area-light responses using a separate local material copy;
keep water SSR normal work unless its missing direction distribution is independently
handled. Preserve original near/shadow/caustic/parallax and all disabled fallbacks.
Only after source review and matched still/motion/reload quality evidence could an
explicit private consumer be considered. Repeated original/disabled/enabled GPU
and total-frame measurements are then necessary for any speed claim.

Current source/physical assumptions do not meet that boundary for general Photon
water. The appropriate current result is the tested reusable conditional helper
and precise limit, with actual water variance compensation unintegrated/unaccepted.

# ShaderLOD measurement and profiling design

2026-11-08 Pacific. Requested by Philip (VP). **Design only; not implemented or
runtime-validated.** This expands the existing cost-map sketch in place. No
Minecraft client, benchmark, GPU workload, Nsight capture or training was run to
prepare it. Research comprised repository/source inspection and primary profiler
documentation. All overhead numbers below are proposed acceptance budgets, not
measurements.

[STATUS](STATUS.md#latest-outcome-and-next-action) owns current direction, allocation
and retention decisions. [BENCHMARK](BENCHMARK.md) owns supported commands and
performance proof. This document owns the proposed profiling design; proposed
commands here are not operational instructions. On implementation, document the
supported interface in BENCHMARK rather than maintaining two command guides.

## 1. Recommendation for Philip

Build a **development-only cost map**, extending `BottleneckProbe`, `GpuTimers`,
`CpuTimers` and their existing Iris/Sodium/DH hooks. Expose it as a separate
`profile` mode in the maintained benchmark harness, with its own capture ownership
and reports. Use a simple offline report for decisions and an exportable trace for
investigation. Do not put detailed profiling inside normal scored A/B windows.

The first screen should answer: **which named stages cost the most, what features
do they contain, how repeatable is that cost, and what remains unknown?** Philip
should be able to expand “shadows,” “fog,” “terrain,” or “post-processing” into
actual passes and submission work, select an area for investigation, and see the
same categories across the four packs. A cost map is a way to choose work, not an
automatic optimization selector or evidence of an achievable speedup.

Provide three related views with explicit units and denominators:

- **Frame pacing:** total frame-start intervals, their distribution and variation.
- **CPU:** render-thread wall intervals, thread CPU consumption, known blocking
  calls and unattributed off-CPU time; optional sampled worker/JVM detail.
- **GPU:** measured command-stream elapsed intervals by named stage/pass/draw
  group, with feature labels, missing coverage and sampling uncertainty.

Do not promise an additive “CPU + GPU + wait = frame” chart. CPU submission and
GPU execution overlap and can cross frame boundaries. OpenGL timers do not expose
hardware busy time, all queues, occupancy, instruction cost or the critical path.
A shader function inside a mixed pass is not separately timed just because it has
a recognizable name.

This serves the decision after the completed 16-candidate screen: G01–G10,
C01–C02 and N01–N04 remain parked. There is no new optimization in this plan.
The native RTX 5080 baselines were already approximately 2.02–3.38 ms/frame;
small absolute observer costs matter. Reuse the completed [RTX report](../dev/experiments/rtx5080-four-target-audit-20261106/REPORT.md)
and [Asahi conclusions](../dev/experiments/asahi-four-target-audit-20261104/audit-conclusions.json)
as context, not pass measurements they never collected. Current STATUS supersedes
historical recommendations in those records.

## 2. What serious profilers establish as the standard

The useful standard is a navigable hierarchy tied to actual execution, accompanied
by uncertainty and a way to distinguish work from waiting. Adopt these ideas, not
vendor layouts. Documentation below was consulted on 2026-11-08; validate installed
tool/API/driver support again before any later capture.

The common lesson: overview first, exact named scope next, deeper capture only
when needed. Hardware traces and sampled stacks complement lightweight ranges.
They do not justify attributing every millisecond to a feature or multiplying a
pass-time reduction into an expected FPS improvement.

## 4. Architecture and ownership

### Separate purpose, shared harness

| Placement | Benefit | Problem | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Detailed timers inside ordinary A/B scoring | Convenient matching of a pass to a score | Perturbs tiny frames, risks observer leakage and changes the proof protocol | Reject |
| Independent application/launcher | Flexible profiler experience | Duplicates input validation, worlds, restoration and remote operation handling | Reject for v1 |
| Explicit profiling subcommand in maintained harness, backed by existing dev probe | Shared preparation and recovery, clear diagnostic identity, exportable results | Requires lifecycle integration and a distinct result schema | Recommend |
| Optional profiling attachment after A/B scoring | Convenient later investigation of a proven change | Must recondition and revalidate; cannot retroactively explain scored frames | Later convenience using the same profiling engine |

Proposed interface: `profile` selects original native packs and a capture tier;
`profile-plan` (or equivalent dry-run option) validates a plan without launching;
an offline report operation reads saved captures. Final names belong in BENCHMARK
when implemented. A new top-level Python launcher, live daemon or production UI
is unnecessary. Reject candidate/optimization requests in native cost-map mode.

Responsibilities:

1. **Harness:** managed-slot lease, capacity checks, input identity, process
   startup/stop, conditioning, operation journal and restoration.
2. **BottleneckProbe coordinator:** one capture owner, lifecycle, frame-boundary
   arm/disarm receipts, window/tier/cadence and bounded in-memory collection.
3. **Scope registry and timers:** stable integer scope IDs, CPU wall/thread clocks,
   backend-specific GPU queries and explicit missing-result records. Existing
   mixins call this layer; no shader rewriting.
4. **Graph inventory and feature catalog:** captured outside profile windows;
   resolve original archive, effective options, selected sources, active programs,
   targets and graph generation into reviewed semantic labels.
5. **Offline analyzer/exporter:** validates joins and coverage, computes window and
   process statistics, creates report/CSV/trace. It must not silently repair
   malformed or incomplete captures into valid-looking totals.

The coordinator state machine is: idle → leased/prepared → inventory →
conditioning → armed-at-frame-boundary → capturing → stopped-at-frame-boundary →
bounded drain → export → restore/release. Errors and Cancel enter disarm and
recovery from every state. A graph reload, dimension/pack change, lost context or
unbalanced scope ends the current cohort; never merge old queries into a new graph.

Keep the existing measurement guard's protections, but distinguish a diagnostic
owner from a scored owner. Before scoring, verify **effective** timer state,
work-witness state, pending collector/drain activity and outstanding image leases,
not just requested flags. No diagnostic query polling, file writer, JFR session,
external capture or observer is allowed to survive into scored timing. Preserve
whatever minimal scoring instrumentation BENCHMARK already requires; this plan
adds none to its scored intervals. GPU/CPU latches take effect at boundaries,
so a request to turn off is not sufficient acknowledgment.

## 5. What “individual features” means

### Physical scopes first, semantic features second

Maintain two structures, not one ambiguous tree:

- **Execution hierarchy:** context → frame submission → stage → program/pass →
  invocation → draw/dispatch/copy/mip group. This has measured intervals.
- **Feature catalog:** named concerns such as bloom, shadows, fog and water, linked
  many-to-many to those scopes. This has evidence and attribution limits.

A pass key includes pack archive identity, effective options/preset, dimension,
Iris version, graph generation, stage/program and source identity. A GL program
number alone is unstable after reload; a string like `composite4` is not a global
feature name. Record invocation and parent IDs because the same name can recur.
Preserve actual viewport/target dimensions, resource roles and draw/dispatch kind.
Inventory source/target metadata once while disarmed; don't query GL state or
reparse shader text at each draw. Invalidate cached identity when the graph changes.

A reviewed catalog entry contains feature ID/display name, matching graph/program
identity, option/dimension conditions, source-member/include evidence, resource
producer/consumer roles, mapping revision and confidence. Labels may be shared
across packs; mappings must be versioned per family and style. This is pack-specific
**descriptive metadata**, not pack-specific optimization code. Unknown versions
still get raw pass names and an `unmapped` label; they do not inherit a guessed map.

### Initial source-backed mapping seeds

The original local archives were read without compiling or running them:
Complementary Reimagined/Unbound r5.9.3, BSL 10.1.8 and MakeUp Ultra Fast 9.5g under
`dependencies/upstream/other-pack-research/`. The following are source-location
seeds, **not a certified inventory of enabled/executed features**. Recheck effective
preprocessing, both vertex and fragment stages, compute stages and the observed
graph before activating any catalog match. Source includes alone do not establish
branch execution or exclusive cost.

| Family | Useful named-pass seeds | Required interpretation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Complementary Reimagined / Unbound | `world0/*.fsh` delegates to `program/*.glsl`. `deferred1` contains SSAO logic and atmosphere/material work; `composite` contains cloud/reflection/material paths; `composite1` includes volumetric light, shadow sampling, water fog/refraction and reflection blur. `composite4` builds bloom tiles; `composite5` combines bloom; `composite6` has TAA and `composite7` conditional FXAA. | Keep both style identities even where sources resemble each other. Bloom fog can move among passes with options; never infer one immutable location. Deferred/composite costs often remain mixed. LPV/voxel lighting needs actual enabled producer/propagation/consumer inventory, including compute if present. |
| BSL | `program/deferred.glsl` produces AO; `deferred1` contains AO use and atmosphere/cloud work. `composite` contains light-shaft/water-fog paths. `composite4` builds bloom tiles and `composite5` consumes them with other post work. `composite6` includes FXAA; `composite7` conditional TAA. | Distinguish AO production from later consumption. The audit explicitly found native FXAA work and temporal writes in other composites; a pass that looks like a copy is not necessarily disposable or featureless. |
| MakeUp | `common/deferred_fragment.glsl` contains AO and volumetric clouds. `composite_fragment.glsl` includes volumetric light and bloom-source work. `composite1_fragment.glsl` includes bloom/blur; `composite2_fragment.glsl` contains TAA/motion-blur paths; `final_fragment.glsl` includes tone mapping and optional final effects. | Preserve mixed AO/cloud and temporal costs. For SSR/water and shadow filtering, inspect `gbuffers_*` and their includes as
well as deferred/composite stages. Actual program bindings under terrain and
buffered draws connect these shaders to runtime scope IDs. Never label all
`gbuffers_water` time “SSR”: shading, refraction, fog and reflection can share that
program. Likewise, do not call all of shadow-map generation “shadow filtering.”

### Required vocabulary and achievable resolution

| Feature/stage Philip can select | v1 measurement boundary | What cannot be isolated by that boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Shadows | Shadow-map root, world/shadow terrain and buffered draws; separate identified shadow composites | Filtering/PCF/PCSS embedded in terrain, water or lighting shaders remains part of mixed passes |
| G-buffer / deferred lighting | Actual `gbuffers_*` program groups and deferred passes | Per-material shader branches unless they are already separate draws/programs |
| SSAO / GTAO | AO producer/filter passes where distinct; named consumers | AO mixed with clouds/lighting is tagged, not allocated a fabricated fraction; do not rename SSAO as GTAO |
| Volumetric / LPV fog | Named volume/voxel/propagation/resolve passes if enabled, including dispatches | LPV is not assumed present; inlined fog/filter costs are mixed |
| Clouds | Cloud producer/history/filter/compose passes and embedded cloud paths | Cloud marching in a mixed shader cannot have its own timer |
| SSR / reflections | Trace, history, blur and resolve scopes where separate; mixed water/material programs | Ray-march cost and reflection-only percentage inside a combined draw |
| Bloom / AA / upsample | Producer tiles/mips, combine, TAA/history, FXAA and actual upsample/blit stages | Native AA stays unchanged; an upsample stage is not assumed just to fill a row |
| Water / translucency | Vanilla and DH translucent terrain, buffered transparency groups and active programs | Water versus glass inside one batch; overlapping feature tags are not additive |
| Vanilla vs DH terrain | Independent world/shadow opaque/translucent roots, DH total and render-list CPU | DH worker work or compatibility when DH is absent; opaque+cutout remains grouped until measured separately |
| Entities / block entities | CPU builds and GPU buffered flush groups | GPU time per entity inferred from vertex building |
| Copies / blits / clears / mips | Actual operation sites, grouped by source/destination/role | Hardware bandwidth or “wasted” work; a long copy interval may include dependencies |
| CPU renderer / submission / presentation | Sodium setup/fill/execute/submit, Iris orchestration, swap, event poll, limiter; explicit known waits | Driver-internal execution, worker critical path and GPU idle without further evidence |

### Mixed and spanning features

A dedicated feature pass can contribute its measured interval once to that
feature. A feature spanning several dedicated nonoverlapping passes can have a
union cost for the same sampled frame. Its shared passes appear as separate
“contains this feature” rows. A mixed pass gets a stable composite label, for
example “AO + clouds,” and lists both tags. Do not split by source lines, texture
reads, branch counts, guessed weights or catalog author preference.

Feature search results may overlap; disable additive totals across overlapping
tags. The accounting view assigns each exclusive physical interval exactly once,
including explicit mixed and unmapped rows. “Time in passes containing fog” is
not “fog costs this much.” Turning fog off would change shaders, caches, history
and output; such an ablation is a separate future experiment, not v1 attribution
and not proof of independent removable cost. No feature toggles or synthetic
shader splitting are part of native captures.

Per-draw detail is bounded: fullscreen passes and copies often already have a
useful single-action boundary. Terrain multidraw and entity batches stay groups
in the default tier. A focused capture may inspect selected draw invocations;
it must not expand or split a multidraw to manufacture individual timings. Full
hardware draw/wave attribution belongs to supported external tools.

## 6. Measurement semantics and data contract

### Records

Use a versioned canonical JSON manifest plus bounded event tables; keep integer
nanoseconds until display. Exported IDs must be joinable without parsing names.

| Record | Minimum fields |
| --- | --- |
| Capture/cohort | Schema/tool/source versions, capture/run/process ID, operation receipt, native/absent/installed-Off identity, archive/options/resource-pack identity, preset, dimension, scene/world/camera, native resolution/AA, Iris/Sodium/DH/mod/JDK versions, GPU/driver/OS/Mesa/kernel, actual GL context, vsync/cap/display/compositor, graph/catalog revision, tier and sampling seed/cadence, restoration status |
| Window/frame | Window/epoch/frame ID; frame-start and next-start monotonic times; root boundaries; graph generation; warmup/partial/transition flags; sampled scope-set IDs and eligibility; end reason |
| Scope/invocation | Registered ID/name, parent/event ID, execution ordinal, stage/program identity, operation kind, thread/context ID, feature links and confidence, expected/observed status |
| CPU event | Wall start/end, thread CPU delta or null, clock source/resolution, sampling state; known wait-site classification and evidence level |
| GPU event | Issue frame/epoch, retrieval frame, begin/end query values when timestamps exist, elapsed duration, clock domain/counter width, backend, context, scope/invocation, availability/validity reason |
| Coverage/health | Eligible/executed/scheduled/issued/completed counts, scope and query-pool limits, conflicts, queue evictions, timeout/reset/disjoint indicators if available, unresolved tail, imbalanced scopes, timer overhead diagnostics, dropped bytes/events |
| Aggregate | Cohort/scope/metric/denominator, frames/windows/processes represented, mean/median/p95/SD/variance, missingness, inclusion policy, attribution grade and uncertainty |

Use explicit statuses: measured, unsampled, not executed, disabled by verified
configuration, not applicable, unsupported, conflict, dropped, pending,
invalid and unknown. Zero is reserved for a valid measured duration (possibly
below clock resolution) or a separately identified structural absence. An absent
CSV row is never automatically a zero-cost frame. CPU thread time unavailable
must remain null, not zero CPU activity.

### CPU accounting

For a same-thread scope, `wall = end - start`; thread CPU is the corresponding
current-thread clock delta. `wall - thread CPU` is **off-CPU/unattributed wall
time**, not automatically GPU wait. Clock resolution can create tiny negative
differences; report tolerance/invalidity rather than hiding large discrepancies.
This difference does not locate waiting inside the interval.

Split the pinned window implementation's swap call and event polling under the
existing parent. Report swap-call wall and thread CPU separately. A long swap call
may reflect vsync, the compositor, queue throttling or GPU completion; label its
off-CPU difference a swap-blocking estimate with cause unknown. Limiter/sleep is
separate. Instrument known fence/resource/query wait sites only where present;
do not insert new fences to discover waiting. A driver may also busy-spin, so
high thread CPU in a GL call is not necessarily useful Java work.

Use JFR or a separate sampled CPU capture for GC pauses, JIT, workers, scheduling
and native stacks. Whole-process CPU includes multiple cores and can exceed wall
time; it is not a render-thread slice. Whole-window worker CPU deltas do not
identify which frame needed that worker. Keep thresholded JFR waits and sampled
stack shares separate from measured scope durations and from one another.

### GPU accounting

Timestamp endpoints delimit command-stream completion progress, not exact shader
execution start/stop on every GPU unit. Elapsed intervals can include dependencies,
pipeline gaps and interference from other GPU work. See the [ARB timer-query
specification](https://registry.khronos.org/OpenGL/extensions/ARB/ARB_timer_query.txt).
No timer backend supplies an occupancy or hardware busy counter.

For valid nested endpoints on one clock/context, derive a parent's exclusive
interval measure by subtracting the **union** of its complete contained children.
Do not sum overlapping children or subtract a sampled subset and label the
remainder “pure parent work.” Name it “outside observed children,” including
unmeasured work/gaps. Reject broken containment. Same-stream sequential intervals
can form a command-timeline stack; that is not a physical shader-unit occupancy
stack. Overlapping contexts/queues, if later collected, need separate lanes.

Elapsed-only records have durations but no GPU positions. They can rank sampled
scope costs, not reconstruct a same-frame GPU timeline. Parent and child sampled
on different frames cannot yield measured exclusive time. Do not subtract their
means to manufacture a residual; show separately observed rollups and leaves.

### Frame, clocks and percentages

Keep total frame-start intervals as the primary pacing quantity, matching the
standard benchmark convention. It is not GPU completion or display latency.
A GPU query's frame ID identifies submission ownership, not the frame during which
its result was read or its pixels scanned out.

CPU `nanoTime` and GL timestamp clocks are distinct. V1 records each clock and
shows separate rulers with an explicit unknown CPU/GPU offset. Submission IDs
link records without claiming queue latency. Never align lanes by first sample
and silently imply causality. Future correlation needs multiple anchors, offset/
drift/resolution uncertainty and an independently checked method; a synchronizing
GL timestamp read must remain outside representative capture windows.

Show CPU percentages against the named wall interval or thread-CPU total, and GPU
percentages only against a valid same-frame measured GPU root/union. Label the
denominator. A duration divided by frame-start interval is at most an elapsed-time
ratio, not GPU utilization; omit that percentage from the default report. Never
compute GPU idle as `frame - GPU`, GPU wait as `CPU wall - GPU`, or total frame cost
as a sum of CPU and GPU. Uninstrumented GPU space is unknown until supported
scheduler/hardware evidence explains it.

## 7. Capture tiers, sampling and speed budgets

### Three tiers

1. **Disarmed / everyday play:** no profiler queries, polling, exports or overlay;
   existing dev-only hooks return immediately. Nothing is shipped enabled.
2. **Survey:** coarse CPU roots plus sparse named CPU layers and GPU pass/groups.
   Record frame pacing every frame with the maintained minimal boundary collector.
   This is the main four-pack cost map.
3. **Focused detail:** short selected-scope capture with denser timestamps or
   narrower elapsed rotation; optional separate JFR/external trace. Clearly mark
   higher overhead. No automatic full per-draw capture of the whole game.

Initial survey settings to evaluate later: one eligible frame in 16, a maximum
of 64 timed GPU intervals per sampled frame (128 timestamp endpoints), and up to
128 detailed CPU invocations per sampled frame. These are bounded starting
settings, not guaranteed adequate coverage or recommended performance results.
If a selected group exceeds the cap, select a declared rotating subset and count
omissions; don't always keep only the first draws. Allow a separately declared
coarser cadence for expensive thread-CPU reads.

Timestamp backend: preserve nested endpoint support, but choose scope depth and
breadth by tier. Preallocate a globally bounded query pool after graph inventory;
per-name allocation in a hot frame does not scale. Keep at least the existing
delayed-availability behavior. Poll only on permitted frames under a bounded
poll budget. Never block for a result or use `glFinish`.

Elapsed backend: `GL_TIME_ELAPSED` queries cannot nest. Extend the existing seven
rotating categories to nonoverlapping named leaf sets. Keep frame roots and
inclusive rollups on separate sampled frames; subdivide IRIS or terrain sets when
query cost/coverage requires it. Do not begin a parent query that masks all its
interesting children. Preserve protection against another mod's active query;
record conflicts and degrade coverage rather than stealing ownership.

Use a reproducible balanced schedule with a recorded phase/seed. Rotate by
**sample ordinal**, not rendered-frame modulo, as the existing tests require.
Across repeated windows vary the phase or use a precomputed stratified schedule
to reduce aliasing with TAA/history and periodic work. Freeze the schedule within
a window. Adapt cadence only between windows, creating a new configuration cohort;
never adapt silently to whichever pass currently looks cheap.

CPU buffers also need bounded primitive storage, registered strings, no per-event
logging, and no collection-time stack capture by default. Do not perform graph
walks, shader hashing, image readback, serialization/compression or disk writes in
capture windows. Move completed data into bounded storage; if full, record loss
and stop/degrade the diagnostic explicitly. No unbounded queues or asynchronous
writer competing unnoticed with measured CPU work.

### Proposed acceptance budgets and later calibration

Survey target: **at most 1% mean total-frame perturbation** and at most 3% p95
perturbation against matched disarmed controls, assessed separately on each
pack/machine. At the recorded RTX baseline range, 1% is only about 20–34 µs per
frame. That arithmetic is a budget illustration, not a fresh measurement. For
focused captures, aim for at most 5% mean perturbation; above that, retain data
only as intrusive structural diagnosis, not representative costs. Disabled-hook
cost should be unresolved at a 0.2% practical sensitivity target; if the study
cannot resolve that, report the bound as unknown rather than claiming zero.

Later overhead study, separate from optimization scoring:

- Compare identical original input/scene stacks with development hooks disarmed
  and survey armed, in counterbalanced repeated windows/processes. Also compare
  the ordinary minimal collector to the disarmed profiling build to isolate
  dormant-hook cost. This requires prospective matched controls, not subtraction
  of historical absent-mod and installed-mod results.
- Compare CPU-only, GPU-only and combined collectors, then cadences/depths; select
  the cheapest configuration that preserves useful pass ranking and coverage.
  Use the same conditioning discipline and include return controls/drift.
- Measure sampled-frame stalls and following-frame stalls, query retrieval time,
  GC/allocation and tail latency as well as window mean/p95. Sparse perturbations
  can disappear in an average while still changing the GPU pipeline.
- Compare sparse distributions against a short denser capture and independent
  external evidence where supported. Check phase bias and whether expensive
  frames disproportionately lose queries. Empty timer pairs provide resolution/
  cost context; never blindly subtract them from every duration.
- Require observed uncertainty small enough to support the budget claim. If
  between-process noise exceeds 1%, “within budget” is not established. Reduce
  instrumentation, broaden repetition within authorization, or report failure.

## 8. Reliability, capture lifecycle and statistics

Inventory and verify original sources/options/graph before warming. Keep
resolution, native AA, camera, dimension, day/weather and workload pinned using
the existing scene machinery. Record rather than silently freeze Iris animation
clocks/history; world-time freezing does not make clouds or TAA deterministic.
Record actual thermal/power/display context and read-only clock telemetry where
available outside hot paths; do not lock clocks or change personal driver settings
as an implicit step.

Start at a complete frame boundary after conditioning and reset epochs without
unbalancing open scopes. Stop new events at a complete boundary. Drain already
issued GPU queries for a bounded unscored tail, preserving their original frame
identity and recording unresolved endpoints. A drain is a distinct state: it may
poll while no new samples issue, but it must finish before any scored operation.
Keep first/last partial frames explicit. A textual warning alone is insufficient;
the analyzer must enforce exclusions and give counts/reasons.

On timer faults, unavailable counters, context loss or scope imbalance, close only
owned queries safely, disarm and preserve the failure receipt. A CPU-only result
can remain useful but must be labeled partial; it cannot pass GPU capture
acceptance. Keep hardware/context capability decisions local. Do not force a
higher GL context just to make a chart available.

Statistics must distinguish:

- invocation cost from the sum/union of invocations **per eligible frame**;
- conditional cost when a feature executes from its occurrence rate;
- frame-to-frame jitter, variation among window means, and between-process
  variation;
- sparse observation count from total frames and effective independent repeats.

Report mean, median, p95, SD/variance and counts for appropriate metrics. Do not
stack pass p95s into a frame p95. For process comparisons use process-level
summaries; frames are autocorrelated, not thousands of independent experiments.
Optional block-bootstrap intervals need declared blocks and enough repeats;
with two processes, show both points/range and descriptive SD, not false precision.

For variable invocation counts, sample by frame/group independent of duration,
then aggregate per sampled frame. Occurrence rates require a separately calibrated
census or a representative sampling estimate; do not infer them from only
successful query returns. Cross-frame elapsed summaries must list the contributing
windows and assume stationarity explicitly. A drifted window does not supply a
credible synthetic “average frame.”

Initial completeness gates: no unexplained buffer eviction; at least 99% of
issued queries resolve or a clear partial-result status; target at least 100
valid frame observations per regularly active ranked scope across the repeated
capture, spanning multiple windows. These are engineering minimums, not statistical
certainty. Rare/disabled scopes get an explicit status, not fabricated samples.
Report full-frame rollup coverage separately from scope-query completion and from
semantic mapping coverage. If unmapped/mixed/uncovered work dominates, that is a
finding and a reason to improve measurement, not permission to guess.

Restoration remains mandatory on normal exit, Off, Cancel and failed Apply/error:
restore owned configuration/scene/display changes, stop owned collectors and
release leases. Unknown concurrent edits must be preserved under the existing
ownership/CAS rules. Keep query objects and buffers bounded and dispose them on
owned shutdown. Do not kill unrelated processes or delete old captures.

## 9. Exports and the decision report

Keep existing `cpu.csv`, `gpu.csv` and `report.json` concepts, with an explicit
schema version and migration readers for old duration-only captures. Add
`frames.csv`, scope/catalog metadata and a compact capture manifest. Raw records
are the canonical evidence; all charts are reproducible derivatives. CSV needs
proper quoting, defined nulls and integer-unit columns. Late data must not silently
rewrite a previously finalized report; use finalization state and checksums.

V1 report: one offline HTML file with embedded summarized data, searchable tables
and a bounded detail trace, plus CSV/JSON for other analysis. No server, cloud
upload or live overlay is necessary. Keep raw traces/captures in the operation's
owned ignored report tree; commit the schema, renderer, reviewed catalog and compact
findings under the [repository artifact policy](GIT_AND_ARTIFACTS.md).

Required views:

- **Overview:** pack/scene/machine/configuration, validity and overhead-calibration
  status; frame-start distribution and window/process points. Show milliseconds
  before percentages. Display historical baselines only as separately labeled
  context, never as matched controls.
- **Cost table:** named stage/feature, underlying pass IDs, CPU wall/thread time,
  GPU elapsed distribution, samples/coverage, mixed/unmapped status and variance.
  Sorting GPU and CPU independently should make sense. Shared semantic categories
  allow four-pack comparison without assuming identical algorithms.
- **Frame graph and hierarchy:** CPU wall stack with expandable children; separate
  thread-CPU totals; separate GPU command timeline for valid timestamp captures.
  Inclusive parents are context, not additional stacked cost. Keep gaps visible.
  On elapsed-only captures, show observed slices/distributions and a clearly
  labeled cross-frame summary, not a completed stacked frame.
- **Flame view:** instrumented CPU wall hierarchy or optional sampled CPU stacks,
  with units and source clearly distinguished. A sample-count flame graph must
  not be labeled milliseconds or GPU percentage.
- **Trace detail:** adjacent frames, stable feature colors plus text/patterns,
  scope hierarchy, actual program/draw-group identity and sampling/clock limits.
  Link mixed feature rows to all contributing intervals without duplicating cost.

Export Chrome Trace Event JSON consumable by Perfetto for CPU events in v1.
For uncorrelated GPU timestamps, export a separate GPU-only trace with its own
origin and explicit clock metadata; do not put falsely aligned GPU slices beside
CPU slices in a common timeline. Elapsed-only data stays duration tables/counters,
not invented start times. Later native Perfetto clock snapshots/flow events can
support validated combined traces. IDs can link submission to GPU records, but
uncalibrated flow arrows must not imply measured queue delay.

Philip's review should end with a small decision record: selected feature/pass
family, relevant packs/machines, observed cost and uncertainty, mixed/unknown
portion, question needing deeper evidence, and his chosen next investigation (or
“not worth pursuing”). No automatic G-number generation, recommendation of a new
optimization, or retention decision based solely on a cost ranking.

## 12. Risks, non-goals and the proof boundary

The main risks are observer distortion at 2–3 ms frames, timer-driver differences,
non-nesting collisions, silent sample loss, temporal sampling bias, graph drift,
mixed feature labels, incorrect parent accounting and false clock correlation.
Every one has an explicit status or acceptance check above. Query placement can
alter batching or tile behavior even without blocking; a low CPU overhead number
alone does not validate GPU pass attribution. Missing instrumentation is a result
to show, not a reason to fill the graph with estimates.

This system will not claim pixel/HDR equivalence, motion quality, DH/PBR
compatibility, occupancy, ISA cost, memory bandwidth, per-pixel feature cost,
end-to-end input/display latency or a universal CPU/GPU bottleneck from timer
ratios. It will not change original shaders, native resolution/AA, enable an
optimization by default, train models, lock clocks, require a vendor SDK in the
mod, or make runtime adaptive optimization decisions. Detailed instrumentation
must remain absent from production jars, with artifact checks to enforce that.

**Cost map → Philip chooses a question → separately authorized investigation →
existing A/B proof.** A future change still needs the maintained native/candidate/
native-return total-frame protocol, ABBA/BAAB where applicable, conditioning,
drift review, quality stills/motion as required, compatibility and restoration.
All observers/work witnesses must be disarmed before scored intervals. A reduction
in a diagnostic pass cannot replace total-frame evidence or weaken the current
all-four-targets/both-completed-machines retention rule in STATUS.

# Agent operations

## Outcome-driven execution

Read the compact STATUS and latest goal tail, not historical assignments. Keep
objective/acceptance, matched baseline/best result, selected hypothesis, stage,
owner, next decisive observation and restrictions visible in the existing
checkpoint. Do not create another task database. An app Goal label is not live
process state. Native Goals/new user-owned chats require explicit human requests.

Choose work that produces a runnable candidate, trustworthy measurement or a
negative result that changes a decision. Plan the selected candidate through its
actual producer/consumer and recovery path: pinned source → selected archive and
options → exact launcher/profile → driver consumption → still/motion quality →
early original/control/enabled/original-return cost → restoration. Verify a
small complete slice using existing tools; a helper alone is not that outcome.
Batch independent cheap defects in the actual saved plan before expensive work;
see [offline preflight](EXPERIMENT_PREFLIGHT.md). Never claim it validated Java,
rendering, loaded uniforms, resource availability or speed.

For the existing Bliss renderer comparison, [benchmark storage](BENCHMARK_STORAGE.md)
provides the actual pinned recipe's destination inventory, fresh preparation and
finite runner. Check capacity on the destination before copying worlds. Cleanup
defaults off; explicit cleanup covers only newly recorded clones after exact
release, while preserving canonical inputs and evidence. It does not clean old
campaigns or authorize a repeat of a closed trial.

For upcoming 26.2 measurements, use the [rate-window qualification and guarded
source patch](BENCHMARK_RATE_QUALIFICATION.md). It checks the effective expected
cap throughout measured frames and preserves whole-window failures and both
baseline comparisons. Install only after the current frozen attempt's release;
the actual owner rebuilds and creates a fresh admission freeze. This does not
reopen a closed candidate or extrapolate support to other version APIs.

Rank a few independent hypotheses by active cost, plausible total-frame gain,
uncertainty reduction, preparation cost and quality risk. Charge setup, repair,
worker replacement and handoffs to the same attempt. Record start/review time,
next decision and positive/negative actions. Roughly 15 minutes without a
useful auxiliary fix triggers a review: simplify, justify an extension, switch
useful work or surface a real decision. It is not a kill switch for healthy
jobs. After two same-cause failures inspect the whole affected contract before
retrying. Do not build a proof/observer framework or revive closed fixed trials.
A rejected candidate does not finish the project; choose the next authorized
useful action unless the human stopped work or a genuine blocker prevents it.

## Teams and integration

Parent owns decomposition, scheduling, integration, durable state and user
communication. Delegate independent substantial deliverables when permitted,
usually up to four useful workers; no slot-filling quota. Keep the next useful
independent outcome owned. Use native subagents; workers do not recursively
spawn or message user-owned chats. Project roles under `.codex/agents/` inherit
current settings unless the user/project contract explicitly selects otherwise.

Every assignment names deliverable/decision, owned files or read-only scope,
existing entry points and authentic input examples, dependencies/resource owner,
acceptance/negative cases, total budget/stopping boundary and report destination.
Partition shared files explicitly or isolate conflicting edits in worktrees.
Workers preserve others' work and return actual evidence, unverified boundaries,
integration needs and live processes. A worker's completion is not acceptance;
parent integrates and checks the combined result. Use independent review where
correctness, research or performance claims warrant it. Parent schedules the
runtime_operator; source workers report opportunities rather than taking a lane.

When reusing a terminal worker, use the supported operation that starts a new

# Conservative normal-error budget helper

2026-10-05. Source owner `procedural_lod`; bounded mathematical review by
`procedural_lod/parallax_math`. New reusable helper only:
`shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/normal_error_budget.glsl`, scalar/
parser fixtures in `tests/test_normal_error_budget.py`. The frozen procedural
adapter, its builder, manifests, pack options and config transport were not edited.
This helper has **no shader entry-point consumer yet**. It establishes a conservative
quality constraint, not runtime acceptance or a performance gain.

The precise current limit is useful: at Photon’s ordinary three octaves, normalized
amplitudes and normal influence0.04, a0.5° universal normal budget permits about7.20%
attenuation of the last octave but **cannot omit an entire octave**. Partial
attenuation still evaluates that octave’s noise/trigonometry. Do not count it as
work avoidance.

## General policy and units

For a normal reconstructed as `normalize(vec3(height_differences * influence, h))`,
keep the original positive third component `h` and original full-count amplitude
normalization. If omitted/attenuated work introduces a raw XY vector error radius
at mostB, the normalized angular difference is bounded by

\[
\theta \le 2\arctan\!\left(\frac{B}{2h}\right),\qquad
B_{\mathrm{allowed}}=2h\tan(\theta_{\mathrm{allowed}}/2).
\]

`h` and raw-error radius have the same reconstruction-vector units. Height bounds
are in the caller’s height units; derivative bounds are height/coordinate unit.
Angles passed/returned by the helper are **radians**. No camera-distance units,
sampler state or shader pack are implied by the common helper.

Rotate the displacement onto one XY axis, placing the two raw vectors at
`(a-d,b,h)` and `(a+d,b,h)` with2d=displacement length. Their angle is
`atan2(2d*sqrt(b*b+h*h), a*a+b*b+h*h-d*d)`. It is maximal at a=b=0; equality occurs
at opposite XY slopes±d. This is an exact real-arithmetic bound, not a small-angle
linear approximation. Counterexample/equality fixtures independently evaluate
angles using cross/dot `atan2`.

The helper provides:

- `shaderlod_normal_height_error_bound`: componentwise finite-difference error for
  one centered bounded wave replaced by its mean. Invalid inputs returnnegative
  sentinel bounds, requiring full original work.
- `shaderlod_normal_error_radius`: convert componentwise height bounds into a raw
  XY error radius with the original influence. Invalid/overflowed input returns−1.
- `shaderlod_normal_error_budget`: convert an angular tolerance into a raw budget.
  Disabled, near/full, unstable/salient, nonfinite/singular inputs returnzero budget.
- `shaderlod_normal_removal_cap`: cap a requested0..1 omission fraction using the
  remaining budget and already accepted error radii. Zero budget retains full work.
- `shaderlod_normal_angle_bound`: diagnostic angular certificate; invalid/singular
  input receivesπ, the maximum angular bound.

No function evaluates an omitted octave, samples a texture or computes derivatives.
An adapter allocates from smallest-error/highest-frequency octaves, updates the
sum of accepted radius×removal terms, and skips a sample/trig kernel only when a
complete omission is allowed. The first structural octave remains protected by
adapter policy. Proposed fractions must remain **constant across the three height
samples of a reconstructed normal**. Spatially changing the fraction inside those
samples introduces another product-difference term absent from this bound.

Near/full fallback is an explicit boolean resolved by the adapter before work;
this helper does not add a distance policy or consume mod config. Grazing/unstable/
salient risk is also a caller responsibility. The supplied absolute flat-view
cosine is protected through`grazing_floor`; allowable error smoothly increases
between that floor and twice the floor. At floor0.15, all views≤0.15 retain original
work and views≥0.30 use the full angular budget. This avoids seeking work savings
from precisely the grazing region where parallax/reflection mappings can become
unstable. Invalid cosine/floor also keeps full work.

Two explicit1/4096 safety margins cover ordinary error accumulation/allocation
rounding in the host binary32 fixtures. Real-arithmetic formulas plus these fixtures
are not a formal guarantee of every GLSL implementation’s floating-point rounding.
Driver execution remains unverified. Maximum allowed angle inputs are strictly
between0 and3radians to avoid the tangent singularity; this mathematical domain
check does not endorse a large perceptual tolerance.

## Pinned Photon amplitude and slope bounds

Reference source is Photonv1.3b ZIP SHA256
`120897768eaa8cb1f14a3e98f88dff009ae3204ee3b96904a4fe8586edfc1ead`.
`shaders/include/surface/water_normal.glsl` retains SixthSurge/Belmu attribution;
this new common helper copies no Photon GLSL implementation or texture asset.
Pinned settings use three octaves and height variation; original finite-difference
step is0.1blocks in procedural tangent coordinates. Existing runtime controls
remain independent from these source pins.

With persistence p=0.5×WATER_WAVE_PERSISTENCE and N original octaves,

\[
A_i=p^i\frac{1-p}{1-p^N},\quad i=0..N-1.
\]

Require finite nonnegative amplitudes and0≤p<1. Photon’s p=1 case has a singular
original normalization. The helper does not replace that baseline with a repaired
normalization or invent parity. Unsupported/singular sources retain original work.

Photon waveG=(0.5sinφ+0.5)² lies in[0,1], with uniform-phase mean3/8 and exact
maximum derivative|dG/dφ|=3√3/8. For a fixed omitted fractionr and nonnegative
height modulationV, the omitted error field is

\[
E_i(q)=A_i r\,V(q)(G_i(q)-3/8).
\]

Pinned normalized LINEAR/repeat512² noisetex gives a per-axis UV slope bound512.
The pinned PNG/mcmeta/source state is verified by existing source/runtime records;
this helper itself performs no sampler readback. For coordinate-axisj,

\[
L_{G_i,j}=\frac{3\sqrt3}{8}\frac{2\pi}{\lambda_i}
  \left(f_i|d_{i,j}|+2n_i\,512\right),
\]

where f starts0.7×WATER_WAVE_FREQUENCY and grows by1.7×WATER_WAVE_LACUNARITY,
λ starts1 and grows by1.5, and noise frequency n starts0.007 and grows by2.5.
Flow direction/rotation must match the actual primitive; no assumed unit direction
replaces the caller’s actual coefficients. Repeat seams remain continuous bilinear
pieces and satisfy the same Lipschitz bound.

Height variation is`max(0.4, 2noise-0.5)`, giving Vmin0.4/Vmax1.5 and per-axis
L_V=2×0.001×512=1.024. Without variation, V=1 and L_V=0. For a finite-difference
coordinate step h, one component is bounded by

\[
|\Delta E_{i,j}|\le A_i r\min\left[
 V_{\max},\;
 V_{\max}\min(1,hL_{G_i,j})+
 \frac58\min(V_{\max}-V_{\min},hL_{V,j})
\right].
\]

The first term follows from the range of the signed centered wave times
nonnegativeV. The second follows by splitting the product difference as
V₁(G₁−G₀)+(V₁−V₀)(G₀−3/8). Sum nonnegative octave bounds, multiply by absolute
normal influence, then form an XY radius. Radius sums are a valid triangle bound;
an adapter may retain componentwise sums for a tighter bound with separate proof.

At the current512 texture and ordinary parameters, even the first octave’s
hL_G exceeds1, so the tighter slope expression saturates. The per-octave height
error bound becomes1.5A_i on each axis. Using guessed smaller noise slopes would
allow more skipping but would invalidate the quality certificate.

## B16: ideal scalar saturation, conditional sampler equivalence

MakeUp `shaders/lib/volumetric_clouds.glsl:44–84` fetches one animated cloud PNG
per sample for native `V_CLOUDS=1`. Only `V_CLOUDS=2 && CLOUD_VOL_STYLE=0`
fetches a second coordinate; that dynamic mode is outside this candidate. Only strictly positive `current_opacity` is added to `cloud_value`
(:73–74). `density` is set on the first positive contact (:75–78) and remains
unchanged. After the loop, only final clamped `cloud_value` and `density` feed
color (:84–102); final sample position and loop index do not escape.

With finite positive `opacity_dist`, once `cloud_value >= opacity_dist`, every
subsequent accepted add is nonnegative and ideal scalar division yields final
opacity one. The candidate breaks **after** the first-contact update, without changing the
sum, forcing a new density, changing sample positions/dither or touching final
shading. `opacity_dist > 0 && opacity_dist < 1e30` retains native traversal for
unbounded/invalid thresholds. Unknown permission values retain traversal.
This is an exact ideal scalar/IEEE division argument, not a proved GPU-bitwise
identity. Actual GLSL division/lowering can differ near the threshold when the
candidate stops at equality while original continues accumulating. The Python
tests use IEEE arithmetic and do not bound target-GPU error. No numerical ULP
bound or measured imperceptibility is asserted, and the threshold is unchanged.
Actual original/control/candidate comparisons remain required.

## A10 and tails: preserve the complete native operator

Photon `cumulus.glsl:110–132,308–330` evaluates origin-dependent exponentially
spaced density queries with per-origin hash jitter: source defaults six sun
and two sky queries per occupied sample; ground is already approximated from
local density/altitude. Scattering is nonlinear and apparent cloud distance is
another live output. Bliss :365–379 has three lower-detail sun samples plus
conditional inter-layer/altostratus shadow terms, and :337 has upper-layer sky
occlusion. Solas :310 uses **one** two-base-tap low-detail sample for lighting,
with no multi-step nested light ray. MakeUp's pinned path has **no nested light
ray**: first-contact density drives color. That exact A10 target is absent in
MakeUp; it says nothing about other cloud algorithms/packs.

**Rejected representation:** one 2D column value cannot represent light depth
from arbitrary query altitude. A unit-density unit-height column queried at its
bottom needs optical depth one; queried at its top it needs zero at the same XY.
The more expensive height-resolved field remains a possible approximate design.

Concrete cost screen, not an implemented candidate: a 128×128×16 RG32F atlas
storing sun/sky requires 262,144 node writes, 2 MiB before border/padding and
2,097,152 density calls per refresh if each node reproduces six+two native
queries. Trilinear emulation requires at least two bilinear RG lookups per
occupied consumer plus mapping/interpolation/edge-fallback cost. A two-pass
integration variant also needs density production, integration reads/writes,
and correct light/sky directions and slice boundaries; it does not preserve
the native origin-jittered quadrature exactly. Native work is 8 times the
**actual occupied** primary samples that survive native exits, at the already
reduced cloud invocation rate, not 8 times full-resolution screen pixels.
Let Q mean **occupied primary samples**, each launching eight density queries.
If Q≤262,144, the illustrative full field cannot even
save density calls before its writes/reads; Q above this threshold does not
prove net speed or acceptable interpolation. This comparison applies only to
the proposed full-refresh eight-query-per-node variant. Height-resolved fields
with other integration operators or temporal amortization need separate cost
and validity models; none is rejected by this arithmetic. No observed Q is
supplied here.

Solas would replace one cheap native low-detail query with field sampling and
production, so a field needs evidence of very high reuse before implementation.
Bliss's three sun queries lower the denominator relative to Photon, while its
cross-layer terms enlarge the representation. These are specific cost gates,
not final mechanism rejection. Native fields/history in other packs are not
assumed absent from this four-family audit.

Photon, Bliss and Solas already have approximate opacity exits. Removing an
earlier tail under B16 is not exact solely because T is small: accumulated
lighting/depth outputs and HDR phase/sun/ambient terms can still change. A
remaining-radiance bound would be a different B21 proposal and must include
every output, finite HDR/exposure bounds and its own cost. No second candidate
was created.

# Opt-in detailed terrain cap

The geometry prototype caps the **effective** vanilla render radius while DH
keeps its existing long reach. It is disabled by default and requires explicit
confirmation that the current scene's replacement ring has warmed DH terrain.
This is an existing vanilla/DH geometry tradeoff exposed as a reversible policy;
it does not add a mesh renderer or promise a particular speedup.

## Configuration and wiring

```toml
[terrain]
enabled = false
vanillaChunkCap = 16
warmSourceConfirmed = false
warmupSeconds = 30
```

The main ShaderLOD enable flag must also be true. `vanillaChunkCap` accepts
8–32 chunks, and warmup accepts 5–120 seconds. Enable the policy only in a world
whose DH replacement terrain you have inspected and warmed; then set
`warmSourceConfirmed=true`. The acknowledgement binds to the world/dimension instance, Iris pipeline,
camera entity, current 16-block horizontal chunk and vertical section, requested
radius, cap and DH distance. A persisted true waits through initial startup and
warmup before first binding. After activation, crossing a horizontal chunk or
vertical section boundary, changing the camera/world/pipeline/radius/cap/DH
distance, or losing readiness revokes it. Returning to the old position does
not re-enable the cap. Clear `warmSourceConfirmed`, inspect the new replacement
ring, then set it true again. The 16-block cells limit acknowledged travel;
they do not prove coverage within a cell.

The main constructor registers the client event handler once:

```java
NeoForge.EVENT_BUS.addListener(GeometryLodController::onClientTick);
```

`GeometryLodController.status()` exposes active/requested/effective radius,
configured cap, eligibility reason, API failure detail, and stable/warmup tick
counts for a HUD or diagnostic command. `confirmCurrentScene()` accepts an
explicit inspected-scene action using cached live eligibility; it re-arms
acknowledgement without bypassing warmup. The caller sets/saves
`warmSourceConfirmed=true` on success. `revokeCurrentScene()` restores the
original effective radius immediately; clearing/saving the flag makes revocation
persistent. No new shader uniform or sampler is
required. Geometry can use original Photon while ShaderLOD is loaded; that
allows a geometry-only comparison with original shadow/AO quality.

## Behavior

An injection at `Options.getEffectiveRenderDistance()` return applies
`min(originalEffectiveDistance, cap)` only while the cached policy is active.
It never writes the raw `renderDistance` option, `options.txt`, or the client's
broadcast render preference. A manual or server-imposed radius below the cap
remains below it. If the user changes the requested radius while capped, turning
the policy off recovers that **current** value rather than an old snapshot.

Sodium and the pinned DH NeoForge wrapper both read this getter, so DH's vanilla
overdraw boundary sees the same radius as detailed rendering. The policy does
not modify DH128 (or any configured DH distance), its mesh quality, or terrain
generation. It also changes other consumers of the effective radius, including
vanilla fog/entity view scaling; this is a radius policy, not merely a draw-call
cache. Inspect the vanilla/DH seam, water and shadow coverage.

Sodium detects an effective-distance change in `setupTerrain` and rebuilds its
renderer. Use fixed caps and explicit changes; do not tune this value from noisy
per-frame FPS. Initial enable/disable and changing the cap are excluded from
steady-state timings until rebuild/upload and terrain overlap settle.

## Readiness and restoration

At client tick boundaries (nominally 20Hz), the controller requires a loaded
world, an active Iris shader pipeline with a DH terrain program and initialized
DH compatibility instance, and public DH API world/config readiness with DH
rendering enabled. Those checks use the exact pinned Iris seams and cached
reflection handles for the optional public DH API. DH must use its normal
`DEFAULT` rendering mode and its configured distance must reach the full
requested vanilla radius. Debug triangles and shorter DH reach are ineligible.
The hot getter performs no
reflection, config reads, allocations, GL calls, or renderer reloads.

A stable world/pipeline/readiness interval must reach the configured warmup.
Policy/mod disable, DH rendering disable, Iris fallback/failure and unload
recover the original effective radius by the next client tick. World/dimension
identity and camera-cell changes also bypass the cap immediately in the getter,
before the next tick. A getter-observed excursion latches revocation even if the
camera returns between ticks. Null/uninitialized DH API, absent DH, and API linkage failures fail open
with a diagnostic reason. The code never calls Iris `DHCompat.checkFrame()` or
`hasRenderingEnabled()` from an Options getter, because those methods can cause
pipeline reloads.

**Readiness is not a cache-coverage proof.** Initialized renderer resources and
30 seconds elapsed cannot establish that every replacement chunk exists. The
prototype therefore requires the explicit scene acknowledgement and is intended
for inspected, warmed scenes. Travel now restores full detailed radius
conservatively, but movement within a cell, terrain edits, DH mesh-quality
changes, independent render-cache clearing and third-person camera offsets are
not automatic coverage proofs or fully detected invalidation events. Disable it
before exploring uncached areas or changing DH mesh settings. Automatic coverage
verification/recovery is future work. The exact public API and internal seams
are audited in [DH_COVERAGE_AUDIT.md](DH_COVERAGE_AUDIT.md).

`src/devClient/java/com/pp/shaderlod/dev/CameraQualitySession.java` is the integrated
development capture utility. It compiled and completed bounded runtime smokes
recorded below, including the fast lossless writer's 603 native frames; broader
quality acceptance remains pending. The new camera-only observation/contract

The harness addresses the missing moving-camera quality check for original,

## Activation and integration

Only `shaderlod.dev.cameraQuality` activates it. Its value is the path of a
local JSON request, read once and limited to 64 KiB. An absent/blank property
returns `null` without opening files, creating threads or moving the player.
`shaderlod.dev.cameraQualityOnly=true` additionally authorizes stopping this
same client after the final manifest and PNG callback handling. The session
must have acquired its local spectator UUID; a rejected request does not close
an unacquired client.

Both capture classes belong only in the dev client source set; verify they and
their nested classes remain absent from the production jar. The integrated
hooks in `ComparisonClient` have this shape:

```java
private CameraQualitySession cameraQuality;

// In the existing one-time configured block, after scene/control preparation:
cameraQuality = CameraQualitySession.createIfRequested(
        client.gameDirectory.toPath());

// After applyControl() in ClientTickEvent.Post, before normal workload handling:
if (cameraQuality != null) {
    cameraQuality.tick(client);
    GpuTimers.drainSamples();
    CpuTimers.drainSamples();
    return;
}

// At the START of draw(RenderGuiEvent.Post), before hideGui's early return:
if (cameraQuality != null) {
    event.getGuiGraphics().flush();
    cameraQuality.render(Minecraft.getInstance());
}
```

The owner must gate creation of `WorkloadSession` and `BenchmarkSession` when
the explicit camera-quality property is present, and place the tick branch
before both old manual/automatic screenshot schedules. The configured block
must preserve the prepared ShaderLOD settings rather than apply its ordinary
comparison enable/preset defaults. A rejected request must retain
its rejection manifest and must not silently become a benchmark. Use a
dedicated quality launch; do not enable `measureWorkload`, `measureOnly`,
`benchmark` or `benchmarkOnly` in that launch. The ordinary comparison client
still opens the prepared landscape world and applies its existing control.
Original absent-mod runs use the existing `compare=off` dev client.

If launching through Gradle, forward these two project properties explicitly

## Request example and path behavior

This 24-second example starts at the existing noDH shoreline player position.
It is an example, not an executed or quality-approved trajectory. Place it in
an ignored prepared runtime directory and use the same request bytes for all
pack arms. The first waypoint must match the prepared `control.json` position
and yaw/pitch within 0.05 blocks/0.1 degrees. Coordinates are **player feet**;
captured `mainCamera` coordinates include the actual interpolated eye height.

```json
{
  "schema": 1,
  "label": "shoreline-motion-r1",
  "warmupSeconds": 30,
  "fps": 10,
  "pngCompressionLevel": 0,
  "waypoints": [
    {"seconds": 0,  "x": 240.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 680.5, "yaw": -180.0, "pitch": 3.0},
    {"seconds": 8,  "x": 244.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 668.5, "yaw": -165.0, "pitch": 5.0},
    {"seconds": 16, "x": 236.5, "y": 69.0, "z": 672.5, "yaw": -195.0, "pitch": 2.0},
    {"seconds": 24, "x": 240.5, "y": 68.0, "z": 680.5, "yaw": -180.0, "pitch": 3.0}
  ]
}
```

Labels accept 1–64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores and hyphens. The source
is parsed to immutable records; exact raw source bytes and their SHA-256 are
retained. The original request is rehashed with bounded reads once each second
and at finalization. Changing it fails the session.

Waypoints number 2–32 and start at time zero. All values must be numeric and
finite. X/Z are within ±29,999,000, Y within ±2048, yaw within ±3600 and pitch
within ±90 degrees. Segment duration is at least 0.25 seconds; total duration is
20–30 seconds and total travel at most 512 blocks. The frame rate is an integer
1–10, and duration must end on a capture slot. Peak eased movement/rotation is
limited to 32 blocks/s and 90 degrees/s. Yaw is unwrapped along the shortest
arc; long intentional rotations need intermediate waypoints.

`pngCompressionLevel` is an optional integer 0 or 1, default **0**. It controls
only the independent Java PNG writer in this explicit quality session. Level 0
uses uncompressed zlib blocks for minimum compression work; level 1 selects
zlib's fast compression. Both preserve exactly the same 8-bit RGBA values.
No frame-rate substitution or global STB compression setting is used. New
requests/labels and loaded capture bytecode distinguish this writer from the
retained legacy `NativeImage.writeToFile` attempts.

Two optional immutable request fields now define camera-context contracts:

```json
{"expectedCameraFluid":"WATER","rejectFullBlockCamera":true}
```

Add these fields to a full waypoint request after surveying the proposed route.
`expectedCameraFluid` accepts exactly the strings `NONE`, `WATER` or `LAVA`.
Omitting it means record-only; null, booleans, numbers, other names and different
letter case are rejected. `rejectFullBlockCamera` accepts only a JSON boolean,
default false. The root manifest's `camera_contract` records the selected fluid
(null for omitted), rejection flag and limited scope. Existing requests remain

## Output and bounds

All outputs go to
`<gameDirectory>/camera-quality/<fresh-UUID>/`. Prepared game directories under
`run-workloads/` are already ignored. Do not run against a tracked game
directory or add these generated files to Git. The output root must not be a
symbolic link and resolves directly inside the game directory. Labels and
request content never become paths. Filenames are fixed `request.json`,
`manifest.json` and generated `frame-NNNN.png`; the manifest uses a sibling
temporary file followed by replacement.

The 24-second example requests 241 slots, including start and end; the maximum
is 301. OpenGL readback is on the render thread immediately after the frame's
GUI pass. PNG writing/hashing uses one daemon writer with **one in-flight
image**, no queue of native images. The framebuffer is bounded to 4096×2160
pixels by area (about 34 MiB of RGBA source pixels). The fast writer streams one
`width*4+1` byte scanline plus a 256 KiB compressed chunk and 64 KiB file buffer;
it does not copy the full image into another array. Each PNG is limited to
64 MiB, enforced before writing each chunk. The sequence now has a fixed
**12 GiB PNG budget** with capacity reserved before the next capture, explicitly
approved by root for native lossless quality sequences. The cap is recorded in
the manifest. At 2976×1672, 201 level-0 RGBA frames need about 4.0 GB (3.73 GiB)
plus small PNG/manifest overhead. These bounds do not establish that the
requested 10 FPS capture rate will be achieved. Keep the requested rate; any
missed slots remain explicit rather than being silently reduced.

If a render misses a scheduled slot or the writer is still busy, that slot is
retained as `missed_render_slot` or `writer_backpressure`. The harness never
duplicates a later screenshot to fill missing motion. PNG write completion
returns to the client thread and records hash, size, UTC completion and write
wall time. The final manifest waits for that callback, with a 30-second timeout;
the manifest is also checkpointed after every successful write callback.
An unresolved writer remains explicit in the failed report. A timeout can leave
the daemon writer finishing an owned file, but cannot be called completed
capture evidence.

Each captured checkpoint records actual rendered mainCamera position/yaw/pitch,
local player pose, motion tick/delta, planned/observed path seconds, actual
wall time, session render count, Iris source frame counter and frame-time
sources, the dev GPU frame ID, framebuffer size, world time/weather, actual
loaded pack, capture-boundary archive/options hashes and screenshot completion.
Encoding description, compression level, PNG bit depth/colour type and actual
NativeImage format are recorded for captured frames; skipped slots also record
the selected encoding/level. The manifest records the writer class SHA-256,
native integer byte order and image/disk bounds. File hashes are still computed
from the finished file on disk before callback success, not inferred from the
source image or an encoder's byte count.
GPU frame IDs may stay zero if the existing GPU timer is disabled; they are not
a GPU measurement here. Full loaded shader options, mod versions, initial/start/
end input snapshots, class bytecode identity, exact request/config and advancing
shader temporal inputs are retained in the manifest. Archive hashes are checked

second. Mid-frame pack reloads are not permitted and need separate coverage.

Statuses distinguish `rejected_request`, `failed`, `incomplete_capture` and
`complete`. A completed sequence requires every requested slot's successful
write callback. Rejected or partial attempts are retained, not erased. Without

## Isolated lossless PNG repair: source and standalone checks

`FastPngWriter` writes PNG RGBA8 with filter None and no interlace. It uses a
per-file `java.util.zip.Deflater(level, false)` for PNG's zlib stream, PNG chunk
CRC32 over type+data, big-endian dimensions/lengths, and fixed bounded buffers.
The implementation follows the [W3C PNG specification](https://www.w3.org/TR/png/)
for scanlines, zlib compression and chunk structure. No STB global or GL state
is accessed by the encoder. Existing files are refused with `CREATE_NEW`, and
partial failed outputs are retained.

Exact pinned-source inspection used the cached source archive
`/Users/pippo/.gradle/caches/neoformruntime/intermediate_results/sourcesAndCompiledWithNeoForge_0b59334a24bba2bc8765d4735bf44be048d0ff21_output.jar`:

- `NativeImage.java` source SHA-256:
  `7732dd3894faf6ed0928db8e519132b486cf263bfc0b49e15cb4a28e10027792`.
  The `(width,height,false)` constructor selects `Format.RGBA`;
  `getPixelRGBA(x,y)` reads `MemoryUtil.memGetInt(pixels + (x+y*width)*4)`
  and does not assert the render thread. Public pixel reads are therefore
  available to the owned image writer without reflection/private pointers.
- `Screenshot.java` source SHA-256:
  `5ec5a5ee36fb49977454a61ad552666d2b837a488352b83d4e5747843fb5ab43`.
  `takeScreenshot` constructs that RGBA image, calls the existing
  `downloadTexture(0,true)` and `flipY()`. That existing download forces alpha
  opaque. The repair preserves this screenshot/readback behavior exactly and
  does not perform another row flip or alpha transformation.

Native RGBA bytes on the little-endian M3 are returned as the integer
`0xAABBGGRR`, not ARGB. The writer emits its low-to-high bytes as R,G,B,A.
For a big-endian native integer, the session reverses the integer's bytes first;
that platform path is source reasoning, not tested host coverage. A non-RGBA
NativeImage is rejected explicitly. The retained legacy screenshot's IHDR also

# ShaderLOD project overview

ShaderLOD targets general-purpose, configurable distance quality control across
shader packs. Photon is the first implementation and performance proof. The first platform is NeoForge with Iris required. Photon is the
explicit compatibility target, and DH is optional for the mod while included
in the development runtime for compatibility checks.

The initial distance proposal is full quality through 32 blocks, medium quality
through 96 blocks, and low quality beyond that. These are starting defaults,
not a measured optimum. Define distance in camera-relative block units and
use transition bands or stable dithering to avoid a visible moving ring.

## Development sequence

1. Establish a reproducible NeoForge client skeleton and compatible Iris,
   Sodium, Photon, and DH runtime. Add durable goal/team infrastructure and a
   small LOD foundation that can be inspected and tested.
2. Prove one distance-sensitive Photon effect works under Iris with DH absent.
   Compare the same scene with the change disabled and enabled; inspect both
   visual transitions and GPU execution time before expanding infrastructure.
3. Build the Photon MVP around several measured effects. Candidate effects are
   POM/material work, shadow filtering, and SSR. Add validated configuration
   transport and useful quality presets as evidence supports them.
4. Extend LOD to DH terrain/water/shadows and validate the vanilla/DH boundary.
   Keep DH optional and test both installed and absent configurations.

## Architecture boundaries

The NeoForge client mod owns config, loader/runtime detection, and integration
lifecycle. Photon owns explicit GLSL LOD logic through a pinned, maintained
patch or derivative. Iris provides the shader runtime. DH extends terrain
rendering and eventually needs dedicated integration checks.

A Java config file does not automatically become an Iris custom uniform.
Document and test the actual bridge before claiming the mod controls shader
quality live. Shader-pack options can support the first proof independently.
Do not expand into automatic rewriting of arbitrary shader packs during setup.

## Product direction clarified by the user

The intended product eventually supports many shaders through a common Iris LOD
protocol, per-effect configuration and explicit pack adapters. Configuration can
map options, units, budgets, compatibility and defaults. Each shader still needs
reviewed code that avoids effect work with distance; names or preset changes alone
do not establish that connection. Pin and verify adapters independently.

Renderer-specific CPU experiments remain secondary, optional components. They
must not become the product's main abstraction or change sunlight cadence to
manufacture results. No sunlight updates or shadow-map refreshes have been changed;
source cadence investigation only informs possible visibility reuse. Photon stays
the reference implementation. The latest 2026-10-05 user direction focuses
development on general LOD and adjacent work avoidance, reusable integration
interfaces and little discernible quality loss, with Photon as the only supported
shader. Other-pack experiments are retained historical evidence. Additional pack
implementation is outside the current goal; future support still requires each
pack's own compilation, rendering, repeated timing and quality evidence.

## Initial risks

Distance branches may save little GPU work when neighboring pixels diverge.
Some effects cannot safely change samples or ray-march steps without changing
appearance or temporal stability. Loader and renderer versions must be
compatible as a set. Photon may require hardware/driver features unavailable
on the development Mac; record this as a runtime limit rather than calling
static source inspection a rendering pass.

The setup goal establishes an environment and evidence base. It does not
promise an FPS gain, freeze the product's final quality thresholds, or complete
the later Photon/DH MVP.

## Concrete alternative assignment structure

Use three bounded deliverables plus parent integration for the next comparable port; this is a proposal for an explicitly resumed port, not permission to resume paused work.

Prepare independent fixed inputs immediately; leave current JAR hash and real producer output explicitly pending. Return one complete prepared operation after the parent publishes the built artifact. Same 10–15minute review boundary, inclusive of fixes.
3. **Bounded reviewer:** inspect the concrete changed family/transaction contract and affected authentic negatives, preferably while the parent compiles. Own no production edits or launch.
